Job Description:
This role is a member of the Bank Identification Number (BIN) Management team which supports the full lifecycle of network identifiers for the Bank's card issuing and merchant acquiring businesses.  The lifecycle includes licensing, registration, setup, enablement, maintenance, migration and termination.  The role manages BIN related initiatives from intake through implementation in partnership with business stakeholders, card networks, technology,  merchant acquirers, processors and other internal and external partners.
Key Responsibilities:
Manage assigned BIN, Issuer Identification Number (IIN), Interbank Card Association (ICA), Acquirer Reference ID (ARID), settlement account and other network identifier activities supporting issuing and acquiring businesses.
Lead BIN setup, modification, migration, expansion, consolidation, and termination activities, including coordination of required approvals, registrations, and validation.
Translate business requirements into complete and accurate network registration and processor configuration instructions.
Partner with card networks, merchant acquirers, processors, technology teams, operations, finance and product teams to execute BIN initiatives and resolve implementation issues.
Maintain accurate inventories, ownership records, hierarchies, attributes, routing configurations, settlement relationships and supporting documentation for network identifiers.
Execute established control routines, retain supporting evidence, identify exceptions, and enter required metrics into ORCIT within required timeframes.
Maintain procedures and job
aids.
Required skills:
Knowledge of the merchant acquirer and card issuer roles within the card payment ecosystem.
Understanding of BINS/IINs, including issuing and acquiring numerics.
Working knowledge of card payment processing, including authorization, clearing, settlement and routing flows.
Demonstraded ability to manage complex projects or operational activities involving multiple stakeholders, dependencies, and deadlines.
Strong analytical, organization and problem solving skills with demonstrated attention to detail and data accuracy.
Ability to quickly learn complex products and processes and independently drive assigned deliverables through completion.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate requirements, decisions, issues and risks.
Proficiency with Microsoft products.
Familiarity with Copilot and prompting.
Desired skills:
* Experience working directly with or for the card networks, acquirers or processors.
* Background in managing card payment network projects.
* Understanding of settlement between card networks and issuers/acquirers.
* Understanding the card network payment processing authorization flow.

Experience with vulnerability rating methodologies.
Background in Windows and UNIX administration.

Job Description:
Global Markets Risk Management serves as independent market risk oversight of the Firm’s trading activities. The Global Market Risk Stress Testing team within this organization is responsible for the implementation and management of critical enterprise processes and analysis to support the global markets business and senior risk management.
The team is seeking a highly motivated individual to support market risk stress testing, including regulatory mandated stress testing activities, formal and ad-hoc scenario analysis. The candidate in this role will have a wide range of responsibilities from evaluating new and emerging risks in the portfolio to ensuring that the Firm surpasses regulatory expectations. This work will require extensive engagement across risk functions and other partners across the Firm. The candidate will also be a key participant in regulatory exams related to stress testing and will become the subject matter expert on key aspects of market risk stress testing. This role will be expected to support the team’s success through an individual contributor role and will have no formal management responsibilities.
Role Responsibilities:
Support the end-to-end scenario design process
by learning and evaluating the stress methodologies that use the mark shock projections
Effectively designing and communicating enterprise-wide and GMIR requested scenarios to business partners
Partnering with Risk Managers, Counterparty Risk Partners, ESPE, and other forecast teams during the development of market shocks and scenario narratives
Understanding the Company’s risk identification processes and inventory, as well as the GMIR points of weakness documents to design a customized internal specific scenario
Analyze scenario analysis results to better understand the key drivers of the results
Facilitate sensitivity analysis and understanding downstream impacts to losses
Integrating requirements for capital adequacy planning, stress testing, and risk appetite monitoring as defined across key international legal entities
Identification of potential process improvements and implementation of solutions
Support the Scenario Generation governance requirements such as policy and procedure adherence as well as quarterly control evidence throughout the year
Engage with technology and data partners to improve the technology platforms used to manage the processes
The candidate will support the scenario design processes of the instantaneous Global Market Shock Scenario (GMS) as part of the stress testing team.  Duties will include, but are not limited to, collaborating on the development and customization of internally-designed scenarios (including regulatory submission scenarios and management requested scenarios), conducting research and analyzing complex data to support future scenario work, assessing risks of the Company and how these risks may manifest in a specific scenario, communicating scenario requirements to downstream users, facilitating review and challenge of each scenario’s shocks and narrative, and creating presentation materials for various committees. The candidate will be a key liaison with risk partners and forecasting teams across GMIR. A requirement of the role will be to develop executive-level presentations, execute on ad-hoc priorities, and coordinate initiatives across GMIR.

rows.title: Quantitative Operations Manager
rows.description:
Job Description:
The Global Treasury & Merchant Operations (GTMO) Forecasting & Capacity Planning team is seeking an experienced forecasting and capacity planning professional who can develop, maintain, and execute quantitative operational forecasts to support staffing, budgeting, and strategic workforce decision-making. This role is responsible for analyzing operational volumes, building capacity plans, translating forecasted demand into staffing requirements, and presenting recommendations to Finance, Executive Leadership, and key business partners.
The selected candidate must have direct experience in forecasting and capacity planning, with demonstrated ability to build workforce plans, explain forecast drivers, assess staffing impacts, and support executive-level decision-making. This individual will apply forecasting methodologies, workforce planning techniques, productivity assumptions, and advanced analytical approaches to support GTMO operations.
The successful candidate must possess strong executive presence and the ability to communicate complex forecasting, capacity planning, and staffing recommendations in a clear, concise, and confident manner. This role requires frequent interaction with Finance partners, senior leaders, executive stakeholders, and governance forums. The individual must be able to defend assumptions, challenge inputs, explain capacity risks, and influence staffing and budget decisions.
The selected candidate must also be highly organized, detail-oriented, and capable of managing multiple high-priority deliverables under tight deadlines. This person should be able to operate with minimal oversight, proactively manage deliverables, identify risks, resolve issues, and ensure that forecasting methodologies, documentation, assumptions, supporting analyses, and executive materials are maintained in an audit-ready state at all times.
The ideal candidate will have strong problem-solving skills, exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, and a high degree of self-motivation. This individual must be comfortable working in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while independently driving complex forecasting, capacity planning, reporting, and governance routines.
Core Role Expectations
Oversees model lifecycle for line of business models, including volume forecasts and capacity plans
Drives organizational strategy to improve model lifecycle processes
Drives horizontal consistency in model development, visualization, and usage across peer groups
Conducts routine model production and performance presentations with executive leadership
Ensures adherence to Model Risk Management (MRM) requirements
Supports ongoing model monitoring to improve forecasting performance and efficiency
Demonstrates deep process knowledge, operational excellence and innovation through a focus on simplicity, data based decision making and continuous improvement
Ensures proper risk discipline, controls and culture are in place to identify, escalate and debate issues
Delivers results by effectively quality reviewing output
Responsibilities:
Develop, maintain, and execute operational volume forecasts to support staffing, workforce planning, budgeting, and strategic business decisions.
Build capacity plans that translate forecasted demand into staffing requirements, hiring needs, productivity expectations, and resource strategies.
Execute quarterly and annual forecasting and capacity planning routines in support of financial budgeting, workforce planning, and executive decision-making.
Develop executive-ready presentations and communications that clearly explain forecast drivers, staffing gaps, business impacts, and workforce recommendations.
Conduct scenario analyses and sensitivity modeling to evaluate staffing impacts associated with volume changes, business requirements, business growth, process improvements, technology initiatives, and organizational changes.

Job expectations include the ability to recognize all risk categories including credit, market, operational, and compliance.
Responsibilities:
Assists in establishing and overseeing the risk management governance structure for the Line of Business (LOB)
Assists in conducting execution of risk framework activities including monitoring and testing of controls and risk management processes for the LOB
Liaisons with businesses to understand market trends and impacts on portfolio, using knowledge of stress testing and its applicability to risk categories
Ensures adherence to the policies and procedures established by the company
Supports the management of risk requests, breach remediations and providing risk effective challenges for front line units
Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR) Overview
Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR) seeks to deliver effective independent risk management of the activities and processes associated with managing the Company’s capital, liquidity and interest rate risks, including price risk in the CFO managed securities portfolio.  As the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) function covering the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Group, we also bring together a holistic point of view across all seven risk types for the Company’s CFO. The team helps Bank of America grow responsibly through developing our teammates, promoting an inclusive culture, and approaching our work with intellectual curiosity. EFR delivers its mission through a steadfast commitment to its values: cultivating diversity of thought and valuing different perspectives and experiences; promoting learning, fostering relationships and creativity; and developing talent, advancing careers, and creating leaders within Global Risk Management and across the company.  Our goal is to ensure that a healthy and sustainable liquidity, capital, and interest rate risk (IRR) profile is maintained through baseline economic scenarios, as well as during times of market and idiosyncratic stress.
Department Overview:
Enterprise Capital Risk Management (ECRM) is a department within Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR). This group is responsible for providing an independent assessment of Bank of America’s Capital adequacy and the risk to our capital position, as described within BAC’s Risk Framework. The department’s aim is to support Bank of America’s purpose in making financial lives better through responsible growth. This is accomplished by providing an independent perspective on the effective utilization of Bank of America’s Capital resources and ensuring we understand all the risks that could impact our Capital resources. The goal of the department is that a healthy and sustainable Capital profile is maintained through a business-as-usual environment and also during times of stress.
Role Summary:
Operating within BAC’s Risk Framework, understand and drive all components of the end-to-end Capital/Capital Risk management process/program for the Enterprise. As a Risk horizontal team, it is our role to ensure the Enterprise adheres to our Capital Management policy. Key components of the Capital/Capital Risk Management program include appropriate risk identification across the 8 lines of business and legal entities, establishment of effective forecasting and stress testing processes across a range of scenarios, and establishment of risk monitoring processes including the review and challenge of Board and Management Level Risk Appetite Limits for our Enterprise and material subsidiaries. In addition to our key Risk Framework responsibilities, ECRM is responsible for completing our independent risk management mandate including ensuring the Company’s capital calculations (spot and forecasted) are appropriate, including any changes to the calculations, up to and including Basel 3 Endgame and Fundamental Review of the Trading Book.
Key responsibilities:
Review and challenge capital rule implementations (in particular, Fundamental Review of the Trading Book and Basel 2.5 market risk capital rules) in the US and international jurisdictions by executing capital calculation testing and performing review and challenge of regulatory rule interpretations and rule compliance documentation
Assess key drivers in trading exposures and market risk risk-weighted assets under current and prospective capital rules
Conduct and document understanding of the capital impacts from new products and new transactions
Develop and demonstrate acumen for the identification of capital risks and mitigants (including market and economic environment and connectivity to other risk stripes)
Ensure understanding of the business processes that may increase our risk, as well as the mitigants to that risk
Assist in the establishment and execution of all Enterprise Risk Management Program requirements
Coordinate and conduct execution of risk framework activities that are the responsibility of EFR, including but not limited to independent review and risk assessment of front line owned processes (e.g. capital calculation, capital forecasting, etc.)
Conduct and ensure appropriate and adequate documentation for all independent risk reviews and risk points of view, including appropriate escalation and communication to Senior Management
Deliver effective review and challenge of front-line owned processes that generate or impact our risk or Capital position
Draft and communicate executive and committee messaging on a regular basis in a variety of formats, including power point and MS Word
Support corporate-wide risk related initiatives, including regulatory change
Enhance the Risk landscape, by ensuring our balance sheet and business model is appropriately stressed across a variety of scenarios, baseline to bankruptcy (resolution)
Provide subject matter expertise related to Capital risk management process and Capital stress testing to the Risk verticals teams, Corporate Treasury and other partners across the enterprise, in order to drive the execution of the stress testing framework and ensure Risks identified are reflected across all scenarios
Critical success measures:
Deliver against the book of work for Enterprise Capital/Capital Risk Management
Ensure that we are providing appropriate monitoring and analysis that allow us to support high quality risk insights
Connection to and execution of responsibilities of the independent risk function
Core Competencies:

Communication- Can articulately paint credible pictures & visions of possibilities and likelihoods
Resilience- Deals effectively with pressure; remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. Recovers quickly from setbacks. On occasion required to take an unpopular stand

Influencing and negotiating across external stakeholders (regulators) as well as internal groups including LOB Risk teams, Corporate Treasury, GRRP, Audit & Compliance to drive execution

Developing Others- Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing ongoing feedback and by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods

Proficiency with PowerPoint and Excel. Writes in a clear, concise, organized, and convincing manner for the intended audience

Job Description:
Global Markets and International Risk serves as independent market risk oversight of the Firm’s trading activities. The Global Market Risk Stress Testing team within this organization is responsible for the implementation and management of critical enterprise processes and analysis to support the global markets business and senior risk management.
The team is seeking a highly motivated individual to support market risk stress testing, including regulatory mandated stress testing activities, formal and ad-hoc scenario analysis. The candidate in this role will have a wide range of responsibilities from coordinating production processes, assisting in the management and coordination of projects and initiatives with Technology to drive operational excellence, and monitoring controls and metrics associated with our key production processes.
This work will require extensive engagement across risk functions, technology teams and other partners across the Firm. The candidate will also be a key participant in initiative planning related to stress testing and reporting and will become a subject matter expert on key aspects of market risk and counterparty stress testing and reporting. This role will be expected to support the team’s success through an individual contributor role and will have no formal management responsibilities.
Primary Responsibilities include:
Coordinate stress testing requests across various stakeholders, including Technology
Investigate and escalate production issues in collaboration with Technology
Manage initiative requests across the team for prioritization in the annual cycle
Drive business requirements for funded technology initiatives for the team
Support adoption of firm-wide strategic initiative impacting trading and counterparty stress testing and reporting
Monitor and report on key health metrics in the stress testing processes
Required Qualifications:
Incumbents typically have 7 - 10 years of experience in the financial industry, ideally with market risk concepts and stress testing knowledge
Technology related Project Management experience
Highly motivated individual who fully understands the demands of a market risk professional with ability to work in a fast-paced environment
Highly proficient at communication with ability to influence co-workers across our global team and all levels of the organization
Intellectually curious with the ability to investigate and develop root cause analysis for issues and propose corresponding process or technology changes
Effective time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple high priority deliverables simultaneously
Experience with regulatory exams and audit

Job Description:
This job is responsible for defining an architectural vision and solution that supports the strategic outcomes of the Business' Products and Services. Key responsibilities include defining the target operating environment, designing for client resiliency, assisting with solution design, and defining non-functional requirements. Job expectations include working with stakeholders and service providers aligned to the Business' strategic objectives, evaluating the impact of strategic design decisions, and contributing to the architecture roadmap.
The Senior M365 Platform Security, Compliance & AI Architect defines and governs the enterprise architecture for the control and enablement capabilities that underpin Microsoft 365. The role establishes the target state, integration patterns, technical standards, and control framework for Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Information Protection, Microsoft Defender, Power Platform, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Copilot Studio. Acting as a senior technical authority, this architect enables secure data use, governed automation, and responsible AI while strengthening information protection, threat defense, regulatory compliance, application governance, and operational resilience across the enterprise
.
Responsibilities:
Own the target-state architecture and multi-year roadmap for Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Information Protection, Microsoft Defender, Power Platform, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, and their dependencies on identity, data, security operations, and enterprise integration services.
Define reference architectures, service boundaries, integration models, configuration standards, reusable patterns, and architecture guardrails for information protection, compliance, threat protection, low-code automation, agents, and generative AI.
Lead architecture reviews and provide hands-on design direction for data classification, sensitivity labeling, encryption, retention, records management, DLP, eDiscovery, auditing, insider risk, compliance monitoring, and data security posture management.
Define the architecture for Microsoft Defender capabilities, including security signal integration, threat detection and response, exposure management, incident workflows, telemetry, and alignment with enterprise security operations.
Establish enterprise architecture and guardrails for Power Apps and Power Automate, including environment strategy, connectors, data policies, identity, application ownership, Application Lifecycle Management, monitoring, support models, and lifecycle controls.
Define the governed foundation for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio agents, including data readiness, grounding sources, agent identity and permissions, connectors, monitoring, auditability, and responsible AI controls.
Partner with Information Security, Data Management, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, Records Management, Engineering, and Operations to embed Zero Trust, least privilege, separation of duties, policy enforcement, evidence capture, and secure-by-design controls.
Identify and reduce risks from oversharing, excessive permissions, unmanaged applications and agents, inappropriate connector use, sensitive-data exposure, policy gaps, control fragmentation, technology obsolescence, and third-party dependencies.
Evaluate Microsoft roadmap changes, licensing implications, control impacts, and emerging AI and security capabilities; translate them into architecture decisions, investment options, adoption sequencing, and risk-based recommendations.
Maintain architecture health and control metrics and communicate material risks, dependencies, exceptions, lifecycle status, and value realization to technical and executive governance forums.
Required Qualifications:
10+ years of enterprise technology experience, including 5+ years designing or governing security, compliance, information protection, low-code, automation, data governance, or AI platform architectures at enterprise scale.
Demonstrated architecture experience with Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Information Protection, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID dependencies, Power Platform, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, and related security, data, and integration services.
Deep expertise in Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Information Protection, including data classification, sensitivity labels, encryption, DLP, retention, records management, eDiscovery, auditing, insider risk, communication compliance, and data security posture management.
Strong understanding of Microsoft Defender architecture, security telemetry, exposure management, threat detection and response, incident integration, and alignment with Zero Trust and security operations.
Expertise in Power Platform architecture and governance, including environments, connectors, data policies, identity, Dataverse, ALM, application ownership, monitoring, supportability, and lifecycle management.
Ability to design secure and governed Copilot and agent foundations addressing data readiness, grounding, identity and permissions, connector security, prompt and response protection, evaluation, monitoring, regulatory obligations, and responsible AI.
Expertise in architecture methods and artifacts, including capability models, current- and target-state views, roadmaps, dependency and data flows, threat models, control design, architecture decisions, and requirements-to-control traceability.
Working knowledge of Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, APIs, connectors, PowerShell, automation, CI/CD, telemetry, and platform operations sufficient to guide engineering and assess implementation quality.
Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and executive communication skills, with the ability to make complex security, compliance, AI, and platform tradeoffs clear to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Experience establishing platform standards, reference architectures, policy and control patterns, architecture governance, lifecycle roadmaps, and technical decision processes.
Experience enabling and governing low-code applications, workflow automation, generative AI, copilots, or Copilot agents in a large enterprise.
Experience in a highly regulated environment and in supporting technology risk assessments, audits, regulatory examinations, control testing, security reviews, and remediation programs.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, cybersecurity, or equivalent practical experience; relevant Microsoft, cloud, security, architecture, AI, or governance certifications preferred.
Desired Qualifications
:
Strategic, pragmatic, and outcome-oriented; balances security, compliance, responsible innovation, control effectiveness, cost, and operational sustainability.
Demonstrates platform stewardship, proactive ownership, sound risk judgment, intellectual curiosity, and the courage to challenge assumptions while remaining collaborative.
Able to operate through ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and move fluently between enterprise strategy, regulatory expectations, cross-platform dependencies, and detailed technical analysis.
Builds trusted relationships across security, risk, data, compliance, business, and technology teams and influences decisions without relying on direct authority.
Demonstrates disciplined execution, attention to detail, continuous learning, and a commitment to measurable improvement in security posture, control maturity, and governed innovation
.

Position Summary:
This job is responsible for overall portfolio or product set performance and asset quality and may include credit approval authority. Key responsibilities include focusing on but not limited to credit, market, and reputational risk; as well as adherence to credit risk policies and external/internal reporting, including but not limited to Top of House (TOH) and Line of Business (LOB) specific reports or regulatory related reporting. Job expectations include having detailed knowledge of regulatory issues and providing expertise on highly complex transactions to business/support partners.
The Credit Risk Manager is responsible for providing independent credit risk oversight for Bank of America's Real Estate Structured Finance (RESF) business across the United States and EMEA. This role serves as the primary Credit Risk partner on the most complex, high-profile, and sensitive transactions, working closely with Relationship Managers, Credit Product Specialists, and other key stakeholders throughout the transaction lifecycle.
The successful candidate will be responsible for evaluating and approving credit opportunities, providing guidance on transaction structuring, identifying and mitigating risks, and ensuring compliance with internal policies and regulatory expectations. In addition, the role includes ongoing portfolio oversight, market analysis, and active participation in strategic initiatives that support the continued development of the RESF platform.
As a member of the RESF Credit Risk team, the individual will provide credit risk coverage for designated markets and exercise approval authority up to the assigned lending limit.
Responsibilities:
Sets or oversees the ongoing management of risk parameters and guardrails for credit risk while ensuring adherence to risk appetite/limits, and actively inspects and/or designs risk scenarios to implement decisions
Supports or oversees the credit approval process and therefore is accountable for overall portfolio performance and asset quality, including underwriting, structuring and monitoring tasks
Conducts analysis, inspects and/or develops credit risk reporting for specific products, and monitors and reports on key indicators for changes in credit quality to communicate to senior management
Sets or oversees adherence to policy and standards and ensures first line credit officers and managers are appropriately performing due diligence that the risk is within the bank's defined risk appetite, using knowledge of stress testing and its applicability to credit risk
Monitors for adherence to industry risk governance, as well as monitoring for potential operational, reputational and market risk issues
Identifies risks early that could impact the assigned portfolio and coordinates with business counterparts to resolve portfolio issues
Translates and manages plans of action to achieve a goal across varying audiences
Review, challenge, and approve financing requests originated by the U.S. and EMEA Real Estate Structured Finance teams, ensuring transactions are appropriately structured and aligned with the bank's risk appetite and policy requirements.
Partner with Relationship Managers and Credit Product Specialists to evaluate new business opportunities, identify key risks, develop mitigation strategies, and provide transaction structuring guidance.
Maintain ongoing oversight of an assigned loan portfolio, including monitoring asset performance, market developments, underwriting trends, and emerging risk factors.
Prepare and present materials for Quarterly Portfolio Review meetings, including analysis of market conditions, portfolio performance, asset quality trends, country risk considerations, and other key portfolio metrics.
Assess a broad spectrum of risks associated with transactions and portfolios, including credit, market, counterparty, operational, legal, and reputational risks.
Provide guidance on policy interpretation and application, ensuring consistent adherence to internal credit standards and regulatory expectations.
Collaborate closely with Front Line Units and key risk and support partners, including Market Risk, Counterparty Risk, Legal, Credit Review, Appraisal, Compliance, and other control functions.Participate in securitization-related activities, including:Reviewing loans acquired from third-party originators for inclusion in CMBS transactions.
Participating in B-piece investor due diligence and review discussions.Reviewing and approving risk retention structures for CMBS and Single-Asset Single-Borrower (SASB) transactions.
Lead or support strategic and regulatory initiatives, including policy and procedure enhancements, Operational Excellence programs, Matter Requiring Attention (MRA) remediation efforts, market studies, and other special projects.
Mentor and advise RESF team members on transaction-specific risks, underwriting considerations, and risk mitigation strategies to promote strong and consistent credit practices.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with business partners and provide credible challenge on risk issues while supporting responsible business growth.
This role requires frequent interaction with senior leaders across Global Risk, the Front Line Units, and other enterprise partners.
The individual must be able to communicate complex risk and market considerations effectively, provide thoughtful challenge, and influence decisions at multiple levels of the organization.
Required Skills:
Bachelor's degree in Real Estate, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline; equivalent education and relevant professional experience will also be considered.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in commercial real estate lending, underwriting, credit risk management, or structured finance, with significant exposure to complex institutional real estate transactions.
Experience with CMBS, SASB, and structured finance transactions is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated expertise in commercial real estate credit underwriting, including analysis of sponsor strength, property cash flows, capital structures, market dynamics, valuation methodologies, and repayment capacity.
Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including cash flow forecasting, debt sizing, stress testing, valuation analysis, sensitivity analysis, and performance monitoring across a range of property types.
Extensive knowledge of credit risk management principles, regulatory expectations, risk appetite frameworks, credit policies, portfolio management practices, risk rating methodologies, and loss forecasting concepts.
Proven ability to independently evaluate and approve complex credit transactions, identify emerging risks, challenge assumptions, and develop effective risk mitigation strategies.
Exceptional organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to manage a high-volume transaction pipeline, balance competing priorities, and consistently meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple concurrent initiatives from inception through execution while maintaining a high level of accuracy, attention to detail, and sound risk judgment.
Strong project management, problem-solving, and execution capabilities, with a track record of driving complex initiatives to successful completion.
Excellent relationship management and influencing skills, with the ability to build credibility, foster collaboration, navigate differing viewpoints, and achieve consensus across business and risk partners.
Proven ability to communicate complex financial and risk concepts clearly and effectively to senior management, risk committees, and other key stakeholders through both written and verbal presentations.
High degree of professional maturity, accountability, and independent judgment, coupled with a strong understanding of the responsibilities and expectations associated with a senior credit risk management role.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, along with experience using Adobe Acrobat and other analytical and reporting tools.

The Senior Lead Control Management Officer will serve as a key member of the Technology Control Management organization, responsible for strengthening the control environment within the Cloud Platform organization. This role will provide strategic control oversight and risk leadership for enterprise infrastructure services, cloud platform adoption, platform engineering, and control modernization initiatives focused on Control-as-Code, automated governance, and continuous control monitoring.
The individual will partner closely with Infrastructure Engineering leaders, Cloud Platform Engineering, Information Security, Technology Risk, Cloud GRC, Audit, and Control Management teams to establish and maintain a strong control environment that enables secure technology transformation while ensuring regulatory compliance and operational resilience.
In This Role, You Will
Act as a trusted advisor to senior technology and control management leaders in developing risk mitigation strategies for complex infrastructure and cloud-related risks.
Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of control frameworks supporting:
Infrastructure Engineering
Cloud Platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP, OpenShift, Kubernetes)
Storage, Compute, Network, Database, and Middleware Services
Platform Engineering initiatives
Lead the adoption of Control-as-Code principles across Infrastructure Engineering and Cloud Platforms, including continuous compliance monitoring and automated evidence collection.
Propose governance standards and operating models for automated preventive, detective, and corrective controls.
Provide strategic oversight of enterprise technology risk, operational risk, resiliency risk, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Proactively identify and assess emerging risks related to cloud adoption, hybrid cloud architectures, automation, AI-enabled infrastructure operations, platform engineering, and infrastructure modernization.
Monitor, measure, evaluate, and report on the effectiveness of controls and risk mitigation strategies, analyzing Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), issues, control testing, and operational loss data to identify systemic risk trends.
Lead complex risk and control governance activities, including preparation of executive-level reporting, risk committee materials, and regulatory updates.
Provide risk and control expertise in engagement with Audit, Compliance, Independent Risk Management, and regulators.
Coordinate issue management activities, including root-cause analysis and sustainable corrective action plans.
Serve as the control management lead for major infrastructure and cloud transformation programs.
Mentor and guide control officers and virtual teams supporting technology control execution.
Required Qualifications
7+ years of Risk Management or Financial Services Industry experience, or equivalent experience demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, or education.
7+ years of Control Management, Technology Risk, Information Security experience.
Desired Qualifications
Knowledge of IT, information security, and cloud management and control frameworks (e.g., NIST Cybersecurity Framework and 800-53, CIS Critical Security Controls, FFIEC IT Examination Handbooks, COBIT, FedRAMP, ISO 2700x, ITIL).
Strong control evaluation, testing, and/or audit experience, including assessing risk, drafting and executing test scripts, identifying gaps in controls and control execution, assessing issues and trends, and influencing change.
Strong risk and control fundamentals, including a comprehensive understanding of risk types, methodologies, and frameworks for evaluating or testing controls, assessing results, conducting research, and identifying control deficiencies.
Technology risk acumen and a clear understanding of policies and standards associated with Technology and Cyber Security Risk.
Experience leading audit engagements and providing feedback to staff.
Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Experience supporting large-scale infrastructure or cloud modernization programs.

CRISC / CISA
CISSP / CCSP
AWS/Azure/GCP Cloud Certifications

rows.title: Senior Business Analyst, Branded Cards Strategy & Analytics
rows.description:
Wells Fargo Credit Cards is on an ambitious journey to build a best-in-class organization, and Business Analysts will play a central role in shaping the strategy and future direction of the business. As part of our transformation, you'll work at the intersection of business strategy, product, marketing, credit, risk, analytics, operations, and customer experience to solve complex business problems, identify growth opportunities, and develop data-driven strategies that deliver business value.
Our vision is to develop versatile, multi-skilled leaders who can think strategically, analyze business performance, evaluate P&L impacts, and translate insights into actionable strategies. You'll gain broad exposure across the Cards business while building skills in strategic problem-solving, portfolio and customer strategy, business case development, and general management.
Join us for a unique opportunity to help shape the future of the Branded Cards business, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build a strong foundation for long-term career growth.
In this role, you will:
Lead complex profit and loss (P&L) initiatives related to business product and customer performance, marketing outcomes, or operational efficiency while demonstrating end-to-end ownership through ideation, design, execution, and measurement
Develop business cases that require in-depth evaluation of a variety of product variables, trade-offs, and measurable outcomes across multiple domains including marketing acquisition, credit risk, and product strategy
Identify and design creative solutions to complex and ambiguous business problems based on data modeling of product and customer insights using hypothesis-driven approaches
Build end-to-end economic models and test plans to support product decisions incorporating revenue, cost, margin impacts, and marketing investment prioritization
Apply understanding of product variables, features and competitor insights to inform experience design and go-to-market optimization
Monitor post-launch performance and assess impacts to profit and loss, customer experience, and risk posture, recommending course corrections based on results
Collaborate and consult with a variety of stakeholders across marketing acquisition, finance, analytics, risk, product delivery, technology, and operations and prepare executive-ready recommendations
Provide guidance, mentorship, and support in reviewing deliverables for less experienced analysts
Required Qualifications
4+ years of business analysis, strategy, product, marketing, finance, credit risk, or related analysis experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education
Desired Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.
Experience leveraging SQL, Python, Excel, Tableau, Power BI, or similar tools to extract, analyze, model, visualize, and communicate data-driven insights.
Strong analytical, business analysis, and structured problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex business challenges into actionable recommendations.
Experience analyzing credit cards, consumer lending, payments, banking, fintech, or financial services portfolios to identify trends, risks, growth opportunities, and performance drivers.
Proven track record of career growth and advancement, including successful completion of rotational, analyst, or leadership development programs.
Demonstrated ability to apply strategic thinking and data-driven decision-making to improve customer, portfolio, product, and business outcomes.
Knowledge of customer acquisition, engagement, retention, portfolio management, credit risk, fraud, marketing analytics, or related cards business functions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop business cases, present findings, tell compelling data-driven stories, and influence stakeholders at all levels.
Experience conducting customer, market, competitive, and portfolio analysis to support strategic business decisions and growth initiatives.
Proven ability to partner effectively with cross-functional teams and business leaders to drive strategic initiatives, process improvements, and measurable business results.
Demonstrated intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments while managing multiple priorities.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams and stakeholders.
Consulting, strategy, business transformation, or financial services analytics experience preferred.

Please review the following job description:
Cyber Third Party Risk Management (CTPRM) supports the Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program by overseeing related activities and keeping CTPRM operations aligned with current TPRM updates, policies, and procedures for Information Security. In this role, an experienced officer guides CTPRM’s offshore operations team and promotes strong governance and operational discipline. The officer helps manage daily SLAs, escalations, and performance for Noteworthy News Monitoring and Reputational & Financial Risk Assessment and supports the Supplier Master Data framework across all TPRM applications.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.
1.   Support the Director of Cyber Risk Assessment in overseeing all third-party risk management work performed by the Operations team, including Supplier Onboarding & Maintenance and Information Security Risk Onsite and Control assessments.
2.   Oversee Information Security Risk Onsite & Control Assessments and guide the onshore and offshore teammates who perform them.
3.   Support global standards that keep Supplier Enablement and Onboarding & Maintenance consistent across all TPRM applications, including Archer, SAP, and Ariba.
4.   Proactively identify strategic, systemic, and process improvements that make third-party risk management more consistent, effective, and efficient across the end-to-end lifecycle.
5.   Develop training and job aids so onshore and offshore teammates have the knowledge and skills to perform all TPRM Operations activities.
6.   Routinely monitor TPRM Operations’ managed activities, including Service, Supplier, and Parent records in Archer, and prompt fixes for data integrity issues.
7.   Represent TPRM Operations when advising stakeholders, including Sourcing, Business Units, Corporate Functions, and all 2nd Line of Defense groups, on Operations-owned processes and control assessments.
8.   Advise and, where needed, provide effective challenge to Service Managers and Business Owners to ensure consistent adherence to TPRM Operations-owned activities.
9.   Coach and serve as a resource for less experienced onshore and offshore teammates.
10.   Work independently, applying judgment and critical thinking to analyze multiple sources of information.
Qualifications

Responsible for independently evaluating environmental risks associated with real estate collateral, determining appropriate levels of environmental due diligence, and ensuring the quality and integrity of the environmental review process. Provides clear, well-supported risk conclusions and mitigation recommendations to support credit decisions. Manages assignments with elevated complexity, including the most complex environmental matters, and serves as a technical resource to business units, credit teams, consultants, and less experienced teammates.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job.  Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below.  Specific activities may change from time to time.
1. Independently determine appropriate scope and level of environmental due diligence based on property type, current and historical use, transaction structure, identified environmental conditions, and applicable Bank requirements.
2.  Evaluate environmental risks associated with real estate collateral and determine whether those risks are acceptable within established risk parameters. Clearly communicate conclusions and provide practical risk mitigation recommendations to business units, credit teams, and other stakeholders in support of credit decisions.
3.  Develop and oversee risk-based action plans when environmental concerns are identified, including additional investigation, regulatory evaluation, remediation, environmental insurance, engineering or institutional controls, ongoing monitoring, and estimates of potential costs to cure.
4. Order, review, and evaluate environmental assessments and related technical documentation for accuracy, completeness, regulatory relevance, compliance with applicable ASTM standards, and consistency with the approved scope of work.
5. Manage environmental assignments with elevated levels of risk, complexity, or sensitivity, including the most complex matters involving significant contamination, regulatory involvement, remediation obligations, redevelopment, multiple properties, or complex transaction structures.
6. Coordinate with environmental consultants, business units, legal counsel, credit teams, property owners, and other stakeholders to resolve due diligence deficiencies, clarify environmental findings, and determine whether completed work adequately addresses identified risks.
7. Evaluate the quality and performance of environmental consultants, provide feedback regarding the adequacy of completed work, and make recommendations concerning the addition, retention, restriction, or removal of firms from the Bank’s approved consultant program.
8. Provide technical consultation and training to business units, credit teams, and other teammates regarding environmental due diligence, environmental risk mitigation, regulatory requirements, and the application of Bank environmental risk policies and procedures.
9. Maintain advanced knowledge of environmental risk management practices, applicable federal and state environmental requirements, CERCLA liability and defenses, lender and secured-creditor protections, and current ASTM assessment and reporting standards.
10. Assist with the development, interpretation, implementation, and periodic revision of Bank environmental risk policies, procedures, guidance, tools, and quality-control practices.
11.  Identify emerging environmental risks, regulatory developments, and industry trends that could affect real estate collateral, lending activities, or the Bank’s environmental risk management practices.
12.  Mentor and provide technical guidance to less experienced teammates, support consistent application of environmental risk requirements, and assist with the review or escalation of complex assignments.
13.  Maintain complete, accurate, and timely documentation of environmental reviews, risk conclusions, required actions, approvals, and final resolution in applicable Bank systems.
QUALIFICATIONS
Required Qualifications:
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1.  Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
2.  Five or more years of relevant environmental experience, including at least three years of experience reviewing, preparing, or managing environmental site assessments performed in accordance with applicable ASTM standards.
3.  Demonstrated knowledge of environmental due diligence and environmental risk assessment, including the ability to evaluate environmental conditions affecting commercial real estate and determine appropriate investigation and risk mitigation strategies.
4.  Working knowledge of CERCLA and other applicable environmental regulatory requirements, including liability considerations and protections applicable to real estate owners, purchasers, and secured lenders.
5.  Demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex environmental information, exercise sound professional judgment, reach well-supported risk conclusions, and communicate recommendations in support of business and credit decisions.
6.  Ability to critically review environmental reports, regulatory information, consultant findings, and other technical documentation and identify material environmental risks, data gaps, inconsistencies, and additional due diligence requirements.
7.  Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain complex environmental and regulatory matters to both technical and non-technical audiences.
8.  Demonstrated ability to manage multiple assignments, including complex and time-sensitive matters, establish priorities, exercise independent judgment, and meet established deadlines.
9.  Ability to effectively collaborate with environmental consultants, business units, credit teams, legal counsel, and other stakeholders to resolve environmental risk issues.
10.  Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and the ability to effectively use technology and information systems to perform environmental review, documentation, research, and communication responsibilities.
Preferred Qualifications
1.  Bachelor’s or graduate degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, geology, hydrogeology, chemistry, biology, or another field directly related to environmental risk assessment or environmental due diligence.
2.  Relevant professional certification, licensure, or designation, such as Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), or other environmental credential applicable to the responsibilities of the position.
3.  Previous experience performing environmental risk management or environmental due diligence for a financial institution, commercial lender, or other organization engaged in real estate-secured lending.
4.  Experience evaluating complex environmental conditions involving contaminated properties, regulatory programs, remediation, environmental liability, or environmental risk mitigation.
5.  Experience providing technical guidance, training, mentoring, or quality review of environmental due diligence work.

Please review the following job description:
We are looking for candidates who bring both technical troubleshooting experience and a problem-solving mindset. Experience in network administration, cloud administration, server administration, infrastructure operations, application support, production engineering, or a similar technical discipline provides a strong foundation. You do not need to be the engineer implementing every solution. You need to understand technology well enough to follow the evidence, challenge assumptions, connect technical issues across domains, and work with engineering teams to drive problems toward root cause and lasting corrective action.
This role is an opportunity for an experienced technology professional to apply their troubleshooting, analytical, and operational experience to some of the most complex problems affecting production technology. As a Problem Manager, you will work across technical and operational teams to drive reactive and proactive Problem Management, helping identify root causes, reduce recurring incidents, uncover systemic technology risk, and improve production stability.
You will work alongside Incident Management, Major Incident Management, engineering, infrastructure, cloud, network, application, and Production Services teams to investigate significant and recurring issues and drive them toward sustainable resolution. The role requires someone who is technically curious, comfortable asking difficult questions, and able to connect evidence across multiple technologies and teams rather than stopping at the immediate cause of an incident.
A key part of the role is using data and analysis to find problems before they become incidents. You will support thematic, trend, predictive, and proactive analysis across incident, problem, change, monitoring, and other operational data to identify recurring failure patterns, emerging risks, and opportunities for prevention. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills will help turn operational data into actionable insights and focus Problem Management resources where they can have the greatest impact on stability and risk reduction.
Ultimately, this role is about more than managing problem records. It is about using technical experience, data, and curiosity to understand why technology fails, identify where it could fail next, and help prevent those failures from impacting the business.
For this opportunity: Truist will not sponsor an applicant for work visa status or employment authorization, nor will we offer any immigration-related support for this position (including, but not limited to H-1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN-1 or TN-2, E-3, O-1, or future sponsorship for U.S. lawful permanent residence status.)

Designs, builds, and implements enterprise infrastructure technology platforms and systems across cloud, network, database, storage, platform, computing, or middleware domains.
Applies automation, monitoring, and optimization techniques to ensure high availability and performance of infrastructure.
Manages infrastructure engineering projects and processes aligned with organizational policies and regulatory requirements.
Collaborates with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to integrate new technologies and continuously improve infrastructure standards and processes.
Troubleshoots and resolves complex technical issues impacting infrastructure performance and reliability.
Supports compliance with technology strategies, standards, and governance to mitigate risks and ensure regulatory adherence.
Reviews and guides infrastructure designs, configurations, and procedures to support operational consistency and knowledge sharing.
Provides technical guidance and direction to lower-level technical professionals.
Develops technical solutions with deep analysis of infrastructure systems and leads infrastructure processes.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, a related field, or equivalent education, training, and work-related experience.
Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in infrastructure engineering.
Strong knowledge of enterprise infrastructure technologies including cloud, network, database, storage, platform, computing, and middleware.
Preferred Qualifications
Problem Management experience in a large-scale technology or production environment, including reactive Problem Management, proactive Problem Management, root cause analysis, and corrective action management.
Hands-on technical troubleshooting experience in one or more disciplines such as network administration, cloud administration, server administration, infrastructure operations, application support, database administration, Site Reliability Engineering, or production engineering.
Demonstrated ability to investigate complex or recurring technology issues, analyze technical evidence, challenge assumptions, and work across multiple engineering teams to identify underlying and contributing causes.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with experience analyzing incident, problem, change, monitoring, observability, or other operational data to identify patterns, trends, concentrations of risk, and potential areas for proactive investigation.
Experience supporting thematic, trend, predictive, or proactive analysis to identify systemic technology issues and risks that may extend beyond an individual incident or application.
Ability to translate complex technical findings into clear problem statements, risk implications, and actionable recommendations for both technical teams and technology leadership.
Experience working across Incident Management, Major Incident Management, Change Management, Event Management, engineering, infrastructure, and Production Services teams to drive problems toward sustainable resolution.

rows.description:
Important Application Submission Information
In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Sunday, November 29, 2026
More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.
Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.
The Project Manager II provides an opportunity to lead technically complex capital projects supporting coal and natural gas generation, including Combustion Turbine (CT) and Combined Cycle (CC) facilities. Projects may span mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and controls, civil/structural, environmental, and balance-of-plant systems within operating generating facilities.
The role is well suited for a project leader who enjoys solving complex technical problems, leading multidisciplinary teams, and delivering projects from scope development through commissioning and turnover.
Project Manager II (PM-II) position has single point accountability or can be under general direction of a Project Director or Senior PM. PM-II position is responsible for management, or assisting management, of all phases of project planning and execution to ensure project success factors are met. These include but are not limited to scope, schedule, cost, quality, environmental, safety, communications, security, and integration.
The position is typically assigned a portfolio of “White” or “Green” ranked projects per the Project Management Center of Excellence Risk-Informed Project Ranking Process. Higher ranked projects with greater risk may also be assigned when accompanied with an Enhanced Support and Oversight Plan (ESOP).
The position is accountable for a portfolio of assigned projects with Low to Moderate levels of risk that impact various levels of the Company, Senior Management or External Agencies. PM-IIs may be assigned projects with specific risk-informed requirements based on specific experience and skill sets.
PM-IIs serve as unifying agents providing leadership, decision making, management, guidance, coordination, and control of overall projects in accordance with established policies, procedures, systems, and requirements of the Company.
Progression to this level is based on experience, knowledge, skills and abilities, and should align with business unit personnel needs to manage the portfolio.
Locations
Below are the possible primary work locations:
Duke Energy Plaza - Charlotte, NC
Lark - Mount Holly, NC
Buck CC - Salisbury, NC
Dan River CC - Eden, NC
Belews Creek Steam Station - Belews Creek, NC
Responsibilities
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Lead capital projects from scope development through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, turnover, and closeout, with accountability for safety, scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, and overall project performance.
Build and lead cross-functional project teams across Engineering, Operations, Maintenance, Construction Management, Project Controls, Supply Chain, EHS, contractors, suppliers, and OEMs.
Develop and execute integrated project plans encompassing scope, estimates, schedules, budgets, risk, contracting and procurement strategies, equipment/vendor selection, construction planning, commissioning, and turnover.
Apply technical aptitude and critical thinking to understand plant systems, recognize multidisciplinary interfaces and risks, and translate technical information into effective project decisions.
Plan and execute work within operating generating facilities, including brownfield modifications, plant outages, equipment replacements, system upgrades, construction sequencing, testing, startup, and return-to-service.
Manage contractor, supplier, consultant, and OEM performance across safety, quality, technical deliverables, cost, schedule, documentation, and field execution.
Drive project execution through active communication and field engagement, including plant walkdowns, design/project reviews, construction and outage readiness, stakeholder coordination, management reporting, and timely resolution of emerging issues.
Basic/Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree and 5 years related work experience
In Lieu of Degree – HS Diploma / GED -9 years related work experience
Additional Preferred Qualifications
Engineering or other relevant technical degree preferred.
Professional Engineer (PE) license a plus.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification a plus.
Experience with capital projects in power generation or complex industrial facilities.
Experience with power generation systems and major equipment, such as DCS, steam turbines, gas turbines, generators, boilers, HRSGs, emissions control systems, fuel handling systems, and major electrical equipment.
Experience with Balance of Plant (BOP) systems, including mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation and controls equipment.
Strong technical aptitude and systems-thinking capability, with the ability to quickly understand complex plant systems and multidisciplinary engineering concepts.
Experience with brownfield projects and plant outages in operating facilities.
Proficient to demonstrated expertise in Project Management, Decision Making, Critical Thinking, and Problem Solving.
Project-related work experience; Risk Management, Project Leadership, Strong Collaboration, Oversight.

Construction Management knowledge.

The Manager of Interconnection Studies and Compliance oversees the generator interconnection study queue and ensures compliance for customers with generators larger than 250 kW in Florida and the Carolinas, as well as distribution-connected generators in the Midwest. The manager leads a cross-jurisdictional team of Interconnection Account Managers to administer all applicable state and FERC generator interconnection procedures, move generators efficiently through the study process, and ensure studies are released on time.

rows.title: Risk Finance & Analytics Lead
rows.description:
Do your Best Work in Mooresville
This position is based at our headquarters in Mooresville, North Carolina. Our corporate office is a space where you can collaborate and do your best work. Take a walk, grab a bite (or a cup of coffee), work out or get a check-up – we invest in you so you can find your inspiration.
Your Impact
The Risk Finance & Analytics Lead provides strategic, forward-looking financial and analytical insight for Lowe's casualty risk programs. This role develops models, forecasts and decision-support analyses that explain financial and claims performance, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and inform risk-financing, operational and strategic decisions. The role works across risk management, finance, accounting, safety, legal, operations, IT and external partners to connect claims activity and operational trends to financial outcomes. Success in this role requires the ability to move beyond reporting what happened to explain why it happened, what may happen next and what action should be taken. The Lead is expected to demonstrate intellectual curiosity, challenge assumptions, proactively identify areas for deeper analysis and bring forward new ideas, models and analytical approaches. The role also serves as a key risk management business and data subject-matter expert, helping translate casualty business needs and data relationships into scalable data lake, dashboard and analytical solutions.
What You Will Do
Develop and enhance financial models supporting casualty loss forecasts, insurance accruals, budgets, long-range plans, Total Cost of Risk and other risk-financing decisions.
Analyze performance against forecast, budget, actuarial expectations and prior periods; identify underlying drivers of variance and translate results into clear business implications and recommended actions.
Evaluate claim frequency, severity, reserve development, payment patterns, closures, litigation, large losses and other emerging cost drivers across workers' compensation, general liability and auto liability programs.
Create scenario, sensitivity and trend analyses to assess potential financial outcomes, challenge assumptions and support strategic and operational decisions.
Partner with external actuaries to validate loss and exposure data, evaluate assumptions, interpret reserve and loss-development results, reconcile actuarial liabilities to financial results, and monitor emerging development between formal studies.
Develop internal monitoring tools, leading indicators and analytical frameworks designed to identify potential financial deterioration or improvement before it is fully reflected in reported results.
Measure the financial and operational impact of claims strategies, vendor programs, clinical initiatives, process changes and other risk-management investments; develop business cases and post-implementation analyses to assess value and performance.
Produce executive-level reporting and decision support that clearly communicates performance, underlying drivers, outlook, risks, opportunities and recommended actions; translate complex actuarial, claims and financial information into practical business insights.
Serve as a key risk management partner to finance and accounting, supporting the integrity of casualty accruals, liabilities, forecasts, reconciliations, excess recoveries and financial reporting, including applicable financial controls, SOX and audit requirements.

rows.title: Manager, Technology AI Risk
rows.description:
Ally and Your Career
Ally Financial only succeeds when its people do - and that’s more than some cliché people put on job postings. We love this stuff! We see our people as, well, people - with interests, families, friends, dreams, and causes that are all important to them. Our focus is on the health and safety of our teammates as well as work-life balance and diversity and inclusion. From generous benefits to a variety of employee resource groups, we strive to build paths that encourage employees to stretch themselves professionally. We want to help you grow, develop, and learn new things. You’re constantly evolving, so shouldn’t your opportunities be, too?
Work Schedule
:
Ally designates roles as (1) fully on-site, (2) hybrid, or (3) fully remote. Hybrid roles are generally expected to be in the office a certain number of days per week as indicated by your manager. Your hiring manager will discuss this role's specific work requirements with you during the hiring process. All work requirements are subject to change at any time based on leader discretion and/or business need.
The Opportunity
At Ally, we believe AI has the potential to fundamentally transform how technology is built, operated, and scaled. As AI capabilities become embedded across software delivery, platforms, engineering tools, cloud services, and third-party technologies, managing AI risk must become part of how technology is designed, not an activity performed after the fact.
The Technology AI Risk team helps enable the safe, responsible, and scalable adoption of AI across Technology. We work at the intersection of engineering, architecture, cybersecurity, technology risk, and AI governance to identify emerging risks, establish practical guardrails, and embed risk management into the technology lifecycle.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, influencing technical decisions, and helping define how AI risk management evolves in a rapidly changing environment. Beyond administering governance processes, you will help shape the operating model, guide how AI capabilities are designed and controlled, and ensure AI capabilities can scale safely across the enterprise.
The Work Itself
1. Assess AI Technology Risk
Assess the risk of all AI use cases sponsored by Technology and complete the associated deliverables outlined in the enterprise AI governance framework. Results will require an understanding of how capabilities will be built, deployed, and operated; identify material risks and dependencies; and determine whether appropriate safeguards exist to support responsible use.
2. Build & Maintain Reusable Controls and Standards
Help establish and evolve AI risk guardrails, control requirements, engineering patterns, and implementation standards. Determine when existing enterprise controls are sufficient, where they should be adapted, and where new approaches are needed to address emerging AI risks.
3. Cross Functional Engagement with Risk Partner and Technology Functio
ns
Integrate AI controls and model evidence into the software development lifecycle to ensure consistency in control adherence and reduce cycle time. Engage Engineering, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and platform teams to translate risk requirements into practical engineering solutions.
4. Enable Responsible Adoption of AI
Engage with teams early to understand proposed AI capabilities and provide actionable guidance on what must be true for those capabilities to proceed safely. Help teams navigate requirements, leverage existing controls, and solve issues in ways that reduce risk without creating unnecessary friction.
5. Mature Technology AI Risk Operating Model & Governance
Contribute to the continued development of Technology's AI risk management approach, including risk-tiering methodologies, governance pathways, assessment frameworks, monitoring practices, reporting, and decision-making criteria. Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and scale governance as AI adoption expands.
6. Support the Rapid Evolution of A
I
Maintain awareness of new regulatory guidelines for AI and ensure they are incorporated into Ally’s program where appropriate. Stay current on world, national, and financial services events related to AI to effectively lead discussions around emerging risk and provide insights/recommendations on how to protect the organization. Effectively operate in an environment where runbooks or prior knowledge may not exist and apply strong leadership behaviors to navigate the situation.
7. What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means helping Ally move from evaluating AI risk one implementation at a time toward a scalable operating model where appropriate risk management is built into platforms, engineering practices, and technology processes.
You will help establish practical guardrails, identify emerging risks early, and enable teams to adopt AI capabilities safely, responsibly, and at scale while maintaining the speed of innovation.
The Qualifications We Are Looking For
Experience in technology risk, IT audit, cybersecurity risk, or technology governance, with risk and governance work focused on technology (such as applications, infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, data, AI, or technology vendors)
Strong understanding of technology risk, control design, and risk assessment methodologies.
Working knowledge of software development practices, cloud technologies, APIs, identity and access management, data architecture, and modern application environments.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence, generative AI, machine learning concepts, foundation models, and emerging agent-based systems.
Skilled at evaluating technology architectures, pinpointing critical risks and dependencies in AI-enabled systems, and designing practical controls and mitigation strategies.
Experience partnering with technical teams and influencing decisions without direct authority.
Strong critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate complex technical and risk concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven ability to work effectively in environments where requirements, technologies, and industry practices continue to evolve.
Nice To Have Qualifications
Experience assessing AI, generative AI, machine learning, or emerging technology risks.
Cybersecurity, application security, or secure software development experience.
Technology architecture or software engineering background.
Experience with cloud platforms and enterprise technology ecosystems.
Knowledge of identity and access management, including non-human identities.
Experience with AI governance frameworks, model lifecycle concepts, or AI control design.
Third-party technology risk management experience.
Professional certification in IT risk, audit, security, or AI governance, such as CISA, CRISC, CISSP, IAPP AIGP, or ISACA AAIR.
Financial services or other highly regulated industry experience.
Minimum Qualifications
7+ years of relevant experience or equivalent combination of education and experience
High school Diploma or GED equivalent
