rows.title: Operations & Business Management Vice President
rows.description:
The Operations and Business Management VP is a specialized role within Community Investing and Development (CID), which works to advance economic opportunity through impact investing, employee volunteerism, the philanthropy of the Citi Foundation and fulfillment of regulatory obligations including the Community Reinvestment Act in the U.S. The VP is responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, business management, and performance governance of CID's third-party partner ecosystem. This role will serve as the designated Business Activity Owner (BAO) lead across 8 core third-party platforms, managing heightened operational due diligence and lifecycle workflows.
Key Responsibilities:
Third-Party Platform & BAO Governance:
Lead end-to-end operational ownership and Business Activity Owner (BAO) execution across 8 core third-party platforms, managing comprehensive operational workflows and elevated due diligence requirements associated with Level 1 critical platforms.
Cross-Functional Partnership Leadership:
Serve as the primary operational liaison bridging the CID team, enterprise Third-Party Management (TPM), Sourcing and Procurement, Technology partners and external vendor leadership.
Intake & Procurement Lifecycle Management:
Steer end-to-end third-party onboarding, contract renewal lifecycles, and statements of work (SOWs) in alignment with Citi's established third-party processes, reducing cycle times and eliminating cross-departmental handoff friction.
Technology & Sourcing Integration:
Partner closely with Technology leads and Sourcing teams to align technical specifications, business requirements, and integration milestones for third-party platforms.
Vendor Performance & SLA Governance:
Oversee day-to-day vendor service delivery, establish performance scorecards, track operational SLAs/KPIs, and lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and partner review cadences.
Operational Issue Escalation & Resolution:
Identify, analyze, and resolve operational delivery escalations, service disruptions, and contract performance bottlenecks with third-party providers.
Executive Briefings & Business Reporting:
Provide senior leadership with operational transparency on third-party spend utilization, platform milestones, vendor performance metrics, and audit-ready operational documentation.
Qualifications:
Experience:
8+ years of experience in business management, third-party relationship management, vendor operations, technology operations, or strategic sourcing within financial services or complex corporate environments.
Third-Party & Platform Expertise:
In-depth knowledge of third-party operational lifecycles, Business Activity Owner (BAO) responsibilities, enterprise procurement processes, and vendor SLA management.
Stakeholder & Partner Management:
Proven track record of managing cross-functional initiatives across business teams, enterprise sourcing/procurement, technology, and external C-level vendor leadership.
Analytical & Problem-Solving Acumen:
Strong capability to filter, prioritize, and validate complex operational information, resolve partner bottlenecks, and present data-driven recommendations.
Communication & Diplomacy:
Superior written and verbal communication, diplomacy, and negotiation skills required to lead cross-business working groups and executive briefings.
AI Fluency & Workflow Innovation:
Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise generative AI platforms and digital productivity.
Education:

The Business Risk and Control Officer is a strategic professional who stays abreast of developments within own field and contributes to directional strategy by considering their application in own job and the business. Recognized technical authority for an area within the business. Requires basic commercial awareness. There are typically multiple people within the business that provide the same level of subject matter expertise. Developed communication and diplomacy skills are required in order to guide, influence and convince others, in particular colleagues in other areas and occasional external customers. Significant impact on the area through complex deliverables. Provides advice and counsel related to the technology or operations of the business. Work impacts an entire area, which eventually affects the overall performance and effectiveness of the sub-function/job family
Responsibilities:
Help contribute to governance and the facilitation of the execution of the Manager Control Assessment (MCA, i.e. Risk & Control Self-Assessment) as required by the MCA Standard including the assessment and appropriate approval of risk associated with business changes.
Support teams in the quality, completeness, and accuracy of the implementation of the Control Framework, including Risk Control Policy, Control Standard, Issue Management Policy, Lesson Learned Policy and Control Inventory.
Assist in performing a detailed analysis on the identification of issue root cause, partnering with control and process owners to recommendations holistic corrective actions and improvements, provide check and challenge to ensure appropriate escalation in according with Issue Management and Escalation Policies.
Help contribute to the Lessons Learned Policy, including monitoring of control breaches and dissemination and learnings across other business units for process improvement to limit the occurrence of similar future events and where similar risk exposure might exist.
Support the review and challenge process, within the FLUs, on the effective design and management of controls to mitigate risks as required by the Control Standards, including implementation and operation, conducting the control monitoring, handling deficiencies, and escalating issues for resolution.
Help contribute to the timeliness, accuracy and completeness of the MCA through controls prior to the execution of a process (QC).
Assist in the monitoring of the adherence to the MCA Standard through controls after the execution of a process (QA).
Support in dealing with Operational and Compliance Risk in accordance with established Policy requirements.
Assist in performing a detailed analysis to identify, assess, escalate, and manage risk exposures across Risk Categories (Operational Compliance, Strategic, Reputational, etc), including material, emerging and concentration risks in accordance with enterprise Policies and the establishment of Key Indicators to monitor risk exposures.
Assist in supporting Risk Appetite and monitor / assess exposures against this in accordance with enterprise requirements (if applicable).
Be part of the process to identify, assess, record and response to Operational and Compliance Risk events, ensuring these are captured accurately, timely and in accordance with requirements.
Help ensure that adequate governance and training are in place to support management of Risk profiles.
Contribute to the risks associated with New Activities and changes to the Business, ensuring these are well understood and adequately controlled (if applicable).
Support operational risk scenario analysis and stress testing for Operational Risk Capital requirements.
Support with risk and control assessments or coordination for programs within various risk stripes and ensure sufficient subject matter expertise exists to enable management of these risks within the Business (e.g. third party, fraud, sanctions etc) (if applicable).
Coordinate risk and control responsibilities and ensure accountabilities are embedded within FLUs, including providing training and leading by example.
Support with standards and procedures that conform to enterprise requirements and support sound operational and compliance risk management.
Apply knowledge of the business, products or services to identify and implement control points and processes throughout the business.
Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behaviour, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.
Qualifications:
6-10 years of experience.
MS Excel, MS Access, SAS, SQL, Visual Basic a plus. 5+ years’ experience in financial services.
Consistently demonstrates clear and concise written and verbal communication skills
Effective organizational influencing skills required.
Third party vendor management preferred. Demonstrated ability to lead global team efforts
Excellent problem-solving skills Ability to comprehend the big pictures with high attention to critical details
Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategy and process improvement initiatives.
Education:
Bachelor's/University degree, Master's degree preferred.

rows.title: Business Risk and Control Officer - C13 - JACKSONVILLE
rows.description:
We are seeking an individual who is passionate about digital accessibility to join the team as a Senior Digital Accessibility Specialist. This individual will report into the Director, Digital Accessibility Center of Excellence, in Technology Controls, and will be responsible for guiding internal partners in digital accessibility development, testing, and remediation, as well as verifying compliance to WCAG and other accessibility standards in alignment with Citi’s ADA policy. This individual will be responsible for educating others on how to implement and test web pages, mobile applications, emails, PDFs, and other commonly used digital file-types for WCAG compliance. Additionally, the Senior Digital Accessibility Specialist will assist with periodic monitoring and reporting of WCAG compliance, as well as designing test processes and procedures. Across all of these efforts will be work to change the culture of the organization, and update “the way we work” to include accessibility considerations.
The Senior Digital Accessibility Specialist is accountable for succeeding against identified metrics. This individual will regularly assume informal/formal leadership roles within teams and must have strong technical expertise and a desire to learn and teach. They must have the courage to always do what’s right, the humility to learn from mistakes, and the ability to
make decisions in alignment with the risk appetite of the organization to promote sound outcomes for Citi and its stakeholders.
Responsibilities
Act as the subject matter expert (SME) for WCAG guidelines and stay informed of new guidelines as they evolve
Understand how a global matrixed organization operates and functions, and thrive in this type of environment
Focus on highest priority demands while maintaining progress on other important work activities; understand how initiatives support organizational success; eliminate activities that distract from the critical few priorities.
Establish bold performance goals; strive to achieve more than what seems possible and put in persistent extra effort when needed; hold self accountable for exceeding expectations.
Work across the organization to help drive the adherence and implementation of key compliance guidelines including identifying opportunities to increase effectiveness
Provide expert accessibility feedback in the areas of design (UX/UI), development, and testing to teams across Citi on new features and functionality
Assist accountable parties (technology, journey owners) to interpret accessibility audit reports and identify root causes of defect creation and monitor remediation of those root causes
Partner with groups across Citi to share best practices for digital accessibility
Assume the intentions of others are based on common goals and shared purpose, and proactively help colleagues achieve their goals.
Participate in testing and evaluating digital accessibility software
Qualifications
6+ years front end development experience
6+ years native mobile development experience
6+ years of digital accessibility development and testing for WCAG compliance
Experience implementing WCAG compliant technologies using Swift (iOS), Java and Kotlin (Android), HTML5, JavaScript, CSS, Angular, JQuery
Experience performing accessibility audits using assistive and automated technologies such as VoiceOver, TalkBack, JAWS, NVDA, Attest, axe, Access Continuum, and WAVE
Experience integrating automated accessibility testing with unit testing frameworks such as Karma, Selenium, and Protractor
Experience integrating automated accessibility testing within CI/CD pipeline
Experience with the following digital accessibility guidelines:
W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 A and AA)
Section 508
User Agent Accessibility Guidelines (UAAG)
Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines (ATAG)
Experience writing Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) code within HTML
Experience with PDF/UA and PDF accessibility
Consumer-centric; empathetic toward the customer with the ability to put oneself in their shoes
Solid interpersonal skills, with an emphasis on collaborating, influencing, and coaching
Ability to mentor others in methods and techniques for addressing accessibility barriers on web applications and mobile devices and in a variety of forums
Fast learner, with enthusiasm and ability for acquiring knowledge to become a subject matter expert on compliance guidelines and initiatives
Experience working in an agile environment
Experience working with vendors on development and testing for accessibility
Strong verbal and written communication and diplomacy skills, with ability to maintain working relationships across a geographically dispersed organization
Industry certifications desired: International Association of Accessibility Professionals (IAAP) CPACC, ADS, WAS, and/or CPWA, DHS Trusted Tester Training for Web on Windows

degree or equivalent experience

Monday to Thursday, work onsite with your colleagues. Fridays, choose your work location, balancing what your work requires.
The Data Center Vertical is seeking a
Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) – Data Center Systems
who
will lead/oversee major deployment programs while working with internal and external partner groups to create and achieve strategic business goals. Your objective will be to organize the overall team, establish clear roles and responsibilities, and create a high-level workflow plan while developing and managing the master schedule.
In this role, you will manage objectives and influence teams without direct authority, while gaining support and maintaining schedule velocity. You will also leverage product, project, technical and investment steward leadership to ensure the project success. You will be comfortable in ambiguity and an advocate for improving program efficiency and finding ways to scale the team.
You will manage all aspects of projects, from beginning to end, with direct responsibility for project execution while leading a team, or teams, to accomplish specific objectives in a given time frame and with available resources. You will also be responsible for the administration, implementation, and management of control projects and accountable for assigned project’s scope of work, schedule, and budget. Trane always focuses on a total solution to provide our customers with the most energy efficient buildings! This position is eligible for a Hybrid work schedule (3 or more days onsite a week) and will be based out of our Davidson, NC office.

Review project proposals or plans to determine a time frame, funding limitations, procedures for accomplishing projects, staffing requirements and the assignment of available departmental resources to various project phases.

Establish a work plan and staffing for project activities, iterations or phases, and arrange for recruitment or assignment of project personnel.
Analyze project proposals to determine a time frame, funding limitations and appropriate processes for accomplishing projects.
Review/approve the work plan of an external service provider or consultancy contracted to execute the project.
Implement a project communication plan.
Conduct risk assessment and mitigation.
Monitor project activities, ensuring the currency, quality and integrity of information, while providing consistency in content and “look and feel” across the organization.
Generate Cost to Benefit Transparency & Visibility across all work.
Ensure that project goals are in line with business objectives.
Ensure that project goals are achieved.
Assign duties and responsibilities to project personnel and define the scope of their authority.
Direct and coordinate the activities of project personnel to ensure projects progress on schedule and within budget.
Review status reports prepared by project personnel, and modify schedules or plans as required.
Establish standards and procedures for project reporting and documentation.
Benchmark project management performance continuously to identify the potential for improvements and increase capability in project and portfolio management.

BS or MS in relevant Engineering Fields.
PMI PMP Certification required.
New Product (Design, Test, Supplier Readiness & Mfg Integration) Experience preferred.

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic
Program Management Team Leader - Data Centers
to lead, develop, and inspire a team of skilled program managers. This role is designed as a player/coach position, where you will dedicate approximately 60% of your time to coaching, mentoring, and developing your team, and 40% to directly managing critical programs. You will be instrumental in elevating our program management capabilities, providing strategic oversight of all projects, and driving continuous process improvements across the business.
Key Responsibilities
The
Program Management Team Leader - Data Centers
will encompass both leadership/coaching and direct program management responsibilities:
I. Leadership & Team Development (60% Coaching)
• Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of program managers and execution leaders, fostering a culture of ownership, commitment to excellence, and continuous professional growth. This includes organizing, developing, and motivating the program management team.
• Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and performance objectives for the team, providing professional support and delegating with respect and ownership.
• Conduct continuous benchmarking of project management performance within the team to identify areas for improvement and increase capability in project, and Design-to-Order management.
• Support team members through training and development in new processes, systems, and methodologies.
• Cultivate emotional intelligence and servant leadership within the team to enhance collaboration and effectiveness.
II. Strategic Oversight & Reporting
• Provide comprehensive oversight of the status, progress, and risk for all projects and Design-to-Order activities within the business unit, ensuring transparent and timely communication to key stakeholders and senior leadership.
• Implement robust reporting mechanisms, leveraging tools like Tableau or similar, to provide clear visibility into project health, risk management, resource allocation, and key metrics.
• Drive communication and alignment across all stakeholders, proactively identifying risks and removing barriers at a programmatic level to support on-time project execution.
III. Process Improvement & Standardization
• Champion the identification, development, and implementation of enhanced program management processes, tools, and methodologies to improve efficiency, scalability, and consistency across the team and the broader organization.
• Lead change management initiatives for significant process improvements, ensuring smooth transitions and adoption by the team and stakeholders.
• Establish and enforce standards and procedures for project reporting and documentation and governance frameworks for the program management function.
• Advocate for improving program efficiency and speed and finding ways to scale the team’s capabilities.

• Directly manage strategic programs from concept to completion, with accountability for scope, schedule, and budget.
• Lead assigned programs and project teams to accomplish specific objectives within given timeframes and available resources.
• Influence cross-functional teams without direct authority to achieve cooperation and drive program success, maintaining schedule velocity and gaining support.

rows.description:
AD & Associate Actuary - AS07AE
Sr Risk Analyst - KR07DE
We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the
future.
T07 Non-actuary
/
Actuarial Students and Credentialed Actuaries
Job Code KR07DE / AS07AE
“Senior Risk Analyst”
/
“AD & Associate Actuary”
Position Overview
The open role within the Risk and Profitability Measurement (RPM) team is a key position supporting The Hartford's Economic Capital parameterization and capital attribution processes across all P&C lines. This role will have a holistic view of the enterprise's P&C risk profile and partner closely with Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and other stakeholders across the organization, including Pricing, Reserving, Treasury, and Finance.
The successful candidate will contribute to the ongoing development and enhancement of Economic Capital parameterization, helping ensure that the model appropriately reflects underlying risk characteristics. Using Economic Capital model results, this individual will perform analyses that inform capital attribution, Return on Equity (ROE) modeling, and other risk-adjusted performance metrics used to evaluate the relationship between risk, capital, and profitability across P&C lines and products.
Responsibilities

rows.title: Transformation Office Senior Project Manager
rows.description:
Be an essential element to a brighter future.
We work together to transform essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity and health. Join our values-led organization committed to building a more resilient world with people and planet in mind. Our
core values
are the foundation that make us successful for ourselves, our customers and the planet.
Job Description
About the Role
Albemarle is executing an enterprise-wide transformation designed to strengthen performance, protect value and build lasting execution capability across the company. The Enterprise Transformation Office (ETO) is the engine that drives the pace and performance of the transformation: it runs the governance cadence, gives the Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) and Executive Leadership Team (ELT) reliable visibility and early warning, and helps Workstream Sponsors, Workstream Leads (WSLs) and Initiative Owners (IOs) turn plans into delivered results.
We are seeking a highly motivated, implementation-minded Transformation Office Project Manager to join the ETO core team. This is an in-house role modeled on a top-tier implementation consulting profile: you will bring structured problem-solving, rigorous program management and executive communication skills, applied inside Albemarle, working shoulder-to-shoulder with business and functional leaders rather than advising from the outside. You will coordinate transformation workstreams, manage governance cadences and cross-pillar interdependencies, track milestones, risks and progress, prepare the CTO and ELT with decision-ready insight, and turn data into clear recommendations.
If you thrive in fast-paced, high-visibility environments, enjoy making complex things simple, and want to make a measurable impact on how a global company operates, we would love to hear from you.
This position will be hybrid three days a week in the Charlotte office.
What you will do:
Keep transformation execution anchored to the committed value and milestone plan by running a disciplined transformation cadence, maintaining a trusted single source of execution truth in Wave, and ensuring the right decisions, risks and dependencies reach the right leaders, decision-ready, at the right time, so that value is protected and the ELT is not surprised.
Key Responsibilities
1. Transformation cadence and governance
Coordinate the weekly ETO governance cadence, including TO meetings by pillar, TO Finance reviews, cross-pillar and function sessions, ETO working sessions and CTO prep, ensuring each forum has the right topics, pre-reads, attendees and outcomes.
Partner with Workstream Sponsors and Workstream Leads to shape agendas so meetings focus on exceptions, decisions and performance gaps rather than status reporting.
Capture decisions, next steps and owners from governance forums; issue clear, concise follow-up notes and track actions through to closure.
Enforce stage-gate discipline (e.g., progression of initiatives through validation, planning, implementation and value capture gates) and ensure adherence to the ETO playbook, timelines and governance standards.
Continuously improve governance tools, templates and routines based on what works for the business.
2. Workstream and initiative execution support
Serve as the day-to-day ETO counterpart to assigned Workstream Leads and Initiative Owners, helping them plan, sequence and deliver initiatives on time and to value.
Coach WSLs and IOs on building robust initiative plans with clear milestones, owners, dependencies and value profiles; challenge plans to be both ambitious and achievable.
Monitor initiative progress against plan, identify slippage or roadblocks early, and proactively work with owners on recovery actions.
Provide hands-on analytical and problem-solving support to the most complex or at-risk initiatives, drawing in finance, HR, IT, change and functional expertise as needed.
Help the business build its own execution muscle so that Sponsors, WSLs and IOs increasingly run the transformation through disciplined routines themselves.
3. Tool performance management and data integrity
Act as a core owner of the Enterprise tool as the single source of execution truth and early warning for the transformation.
Drive data hygiene across workstreams: complete and current milestones, dates, owners, status, risks and actuals, aligned to reporting deadlines.
Distinguish genuine performance shortfalls from timing shifts and data-quality gaps, and explain variance clearly to leaders.
Build and maintain dashboards, trackers and pipeline views that let leaders understand performance, milestones, emerging risks, decisions and dependencies without manual reconstruction.
Provide guidance, office hours and practical support to Wave users across the organization in partnership with the IT/Tool lead.
4. Cross-pillar decisions, dependencies and risks
Maintain forward visibility of upcoming big decisions, cross-pillar dependencies, risks and key milestones across Specialties, Energy Storage, Enterprise Operating Model and enabling functions.
Identify early where enterprise trade-offs or ELT involvement could accelerate decisions, unblock dependencies or drive adoption beyond the authority of a single pillar or workstream.
Help Workstream Sponsors and champions classify issues: resolved within the pillar, shared for ELT awareness, or escalated for an ELT decision, keeping escalations evidence-based, proportionate and decision-ready.
Coordinate across functions (Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Procurement, Operations, Commercial) to resolve interdependencies and keep execution moving.
5. Executive reporting and ELT / SteerCo preparation
Prepare high-quality materials for ELT SteerCo, CTO updates and pillar reviews, including pre-reads, dashboard summaries, variance explanations, decision papers and recommendations.
Synthesize complex information from multiple workstreams into crisp, executive-level storylines with clear asks.
Prepare the CTO ahead of TO and ELT meetings, highlighting areas to challenge, areas to celebrate and decisions required.
Draft and present updates to senior leaders with confidence, credibility and appropriate business context.
6. Analysis, problem-solving and value integrity
Conduct structured analysis, including business case review, value tracking, root-cause analysis and scenario modeling, to identify key issues and develop practical recommendations.
Partner with TO Finance to ensure financial integrity of the pipeline: validated business cases, accurate tracking of value and cash impact, and timely actuals.
Surface value leakage early and support Workstream Sponsors and WSLs in developing mitigation and refill plans when commitments are threatened.
Solve ad-hoc problems quickly, applying a hypothesis-driven approach and turning data into decision-ready recommendations.
7. Change, communications and capability building
Work with the TO Change Director and Change Managers to integrate change management and adoption into initiative plans and governance.
Contribute to transformation-wide communications, such as newsletters, recognition of teams and individuals, Tool guidance, and updates for WSLs, IOs and broader audiences.
Develop and deliver training, playbooks and practical guidance that build transformation and execution capability across Albemarle.
Model and promote the behaviors of an execution culture: ownership, transparency, pace and collaboration.
8. Stakeholder partnership and team contribution
Build trusted relationships with Workstream Sponsors, Workstream Leads, Initiative Owners and functional leaders, acting as a credible partner who brings facts and asks how the ETO can help.
Collaborate closely with ETO colleagues (ETO Director, fellow TO Project Managers, TO Finance, Change and Communications, HR Business Partner and IT/Wave lead) to deliver a seamless ETO.
Stay current on transformation, performance management and implementation best practices and bring new ideas to strengthen how the ETO operates.
Contribute to the growth and development of the ETO team and reflect Albemarle's values in every interaction.
What you will bring:
Required
Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Finance or a related field.
3 to 6 years of experience in management consulting (strategy, operations or implementation), transformation office, PMO or corporate strategy roles, with a proven track record of delivering measurable results.
Demonstrated experience supporting large-scale operational, organizational or cost transformations, ideally including value tracking and stage-gate governance.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think critically and creatively in complex, ambiguous situations.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint; ability to build executive-ready materials quickly.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complexity into concise, executive-level messages.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritize effectively and drive change through influence rather than authority.
It'd be great if you also have:
MBA or Master's degree from a leading university.
Experience at a top-tier consulting firm or its implementation practice, or in an in-house transformation office of a global company.
Experience with transformation tracking platforms (e.g., Wave or similar) and data visualization tools such as Power BI.
Background in chemicals, materials, energy, mining or other industrial / manufacturing sectors.
Familiarity with change management methodologies and financial concepts such as business cases, run-rate value and cash impact.
Experience working with global, matrixed and multicultural teams.
Skills and Attributes
Executive presence: comfortable engaging ELT members and senior leaders, with the judgment to know when and how to escalate.
Ownership and discipline: brings rigor, holds the line on standards and follows through relentlessly.
Structured problem-solver: structures ambiguous problems, uses data to drive decisions, and moves quickly from analysis to action.
Collaborative influencer: builds trust across pillars and functions; leads through influence, coaching and partnership.
Clear communicator: writes and speaks with clarity and brevity; tailors messages for ELT, sponsors and frontline teams.
Resilient and adaptable: maintains pace and composure across competing priorities and tight deadlines.
Impact-driven: cares about building lasting capability, not just completing tasks.

rows.description:
Be an essential element to a brighter future.

Job Description
Albemarle is hiring for an Area Project Manager. This position is hybrid and located in Kings Mountain, NC and full-time on-site presence is required during active construction phases.
The Area Project Manager – Non-Process Infrastructure (NPI) is a senior capital project leadership role within Albemarle’s Kings Mountain lithium mine project—one of the most strategically significant critical mineral developments in the United States. This role owns end-to-end delivery of non-process infrastructure that enables safe, on-schedule construction and start-up of the Mine, Concentrator, and Tailings areas.
NPI scope includes high-voltage power and substations; mine haul/access roads and site earthworks; raw and process water supply, storage, and treatment; stormwater and environmental containment; site buildings (maintenance, warehouse, dry/admin); telecoms/controls backbone; geotechnical and surveying programs; and third-party utility coordination.
The successful candidate brings hands-on experience delivering infrastructure for greenfield or brownfield mining and mineral processing facilities, with strong understanding of hard-rock concentrator sequencing and interfaces. This role requires an EPCM-caliber project manager with an owner’s mindset to protect schedule, capital, and operability through design, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
What You Will Do
Project Leadership & Execution
Own scope, schedule, budget, and risk for all NPI projects supporting the Mine, Concentrator, and Tailings areas across FEL2–IFC, construction, commissioning, and handover.
Develop execution plans, WBS, and integrated schedules aligned to the overall Kings Mountain master schedule and critical path.
Control cost and change (Class 3 through completion): estimates, commitments, contingency, change orders, and monthly performance reporting.
Maintain risk and issue registers, drive timely resolution/escalation, and lead NPI stage-gate readiness reviews to ensure FEL maturity before sanction and execution.
Mining & Concentrator Infrastructure Expertise
Lead greenfield hard-rock mining infrastructure delivery: access/haul roads, earthworks, ROM pad interfaces, and overburden/stockpile enabling works.
Translate concentrator needs (crushing, grinding, separation/flotation, dewatering) into coordinated NPI scope: power, water, compressed air, reagent/utility areas, and building envelope.
Manage mine-to-plant and plant interface points with process, OEMs, and EPCM: equipment pads/foundations, utility tie-ins, corridors, constructability, and commissioning utility readiness.
Coordinate tailings infrastructure interfaces (ancillary works, return water, decant/pumping, access) with geotechnical and environmental teams.
Engineering & Design Oversight
Direct EPCM and specialty consultants across civil/structural, mechanical, electrical, I&C, and architectural disciplines for NPI scope.
Review/approve key deliverables (site layout, grading, foundations/structures, electrical single-lines, underground utilities) and guide routing decisions to ensure constructability and operability.
Ensure all designs incorporate safety-in-design principles and satisfy requirements identified through HAZID, HAZOP, and constructability reviews. Ensure all open action items are formally closed prior to IFC issuance.
Participate in or lead value engineering exercises to optimize NPI capital cost without compromising operability, maintainability, or regulatory compliance.
Contractor & Supplier Coordination
Manage interfaces with NPI contractors/utility providers and internal stakeholders; ensure scopes, RFPs, contracts, and changes capture technical and schedule requirements.
Ensure commercial documents – RFPs, scopes of work, contracts, and change orders – fully capture NPI technical requirements and are aligned with the contracting & procurement team’s standards.
Integrate OEM/vendor requirements into NPI execution (foundations, heavy-haul access/laydown, pre-install utilities, and commissioning readiness) and drive timely receipt of vendor data.
Permitting, Land & Regulatory
Maintain NPI permitting and land tracker (land disturbance, building, encroachments, utility agreements, environmental authorizations) and align construction sequencing to permit conditions.
Oversee surveying/easements/right-of-way and geotechnical investigations to support design, manage subsurface risk, and enable construction.
Reporting & Controls
Implement project controls for NPI scope (baseline, progress, forecasting, and change) and communicate status, risks, and milestones to project leadership and key stakeholders.
Safety & Compliance
Champion safety-first execution for NPI, embedding safety-in-design and ensuring contractor plans meet site requirements.
Ensure compliance with MSHA/OSHA requirements and track closure of hazard review and PHA action items prior to construction.
What You Bring
Education
B.S. in Mechanical, Civil, Electrical, or Chemical Engineering (Mechanical/Civil preferred for mining and concentrator infrastructure scope).
PE strongly preferred; PMP a plus.
Experience
15+ years capital project leadership, primarily in mining, mineral processing, or heavy industrial environments.
Proven delivery of infrastructure for at least one greenfield/brownfield mine development or major concentrator project; EPCM/owner-side delivery experience highly valued.
Demonstrated NPI delivery in a mining context (earthworks/roads, HV power, water/stormwater, buildings, multi-utility distribution) within a stage-gate framework (FEL1–FEL3 / Class 5–2 estimates).
Experience executing government-funded or incentive-supported capital projects (e.g., federal/state grants, DOE programs), including compliance, reporting, and audit readiness preferred but not required.
Working knowledge of concentrator equipment installation interfaces (crushing, grinding, flotation/separation, thickening/filtration, conveying) and associated utility/sequencing impacts.
Experience in the lithium, borates, potash, or other specialty minerals industry is a plus given the Kings Mountain project’s critical mineral mandate.
Technical Skills
Able to interpret and challenge key engineering documents (P&IDs, layouts, grading, single-lines, structural and I&C drawings).
Knowledge of MSHA requirements and strong proficiency with schedule/cost tools (Primavera P6, MS Project, or equivalent).
Leadership & Interpersonal
Lead and influence multi-disciplinary teams in fast-paced, greenfield mining construction environments.
Communicate complex project status and risk clearly; operates with an owner’s mindset to protect schedule, cost, quality, and operability.
Specific Interface Responsibilities
Electric power provider: interconnection agreements, substation/design reviews, metering, and energization schedule coordination.
Permitting: maintain real-time permit status for NPI construction; ensure sequencing complies with conditions and avoids violations.
Land/surveying & geotechnical: survey control/as-builts, boundary/easements, and subsurface investigations to support roads, earthworks, and foundations.

rows.description:
Corp Counsel III (Privacy, Digital Risk, and Cybersecurity)
What you will be doing:
Working as part of Premier's Privacy Office, the Corporate Counsel III (Privacy, Digital Risk, and Cybersecurity) advises Premier on compliance with applicable privacy, cybersecurity, and digital laws, regulations, and industry frameworks, including U.S. state privacy laws, HIPAA and HITECH, PCI DSS, and NIST.
This position will serve as the team’s principal legal specialist for cybersecurity regulatory compliance, while partnering with the Corporate Counsel III (Privacy, Digital & AI) on privacy compliance and digital risk oversight. The attorney will provide practical, risk-based guidance to Premier’s business teams, AI & Data Analytics organization, and Legal team.
This role will partner cross-functionally to continuously improve, operationalize, and evolve Premier’s privacy, cybersecurity, and digital governance programs. The attorney will work closely with the Security and Technology teams to translate applicable regulatory requirements into practical, scalable processes and controls supporting supplier privacy and vendor cybersecurity assessments, privacy impact assessments, privacy-related cybersecurity audit requirements, online privacy and digital compliance, and specialized privacy and cybersecurity contract negotiations. The attorney will also monitor evolving privacy, cybersecurity, and digital legal requirements and advise relevant stakeholders on their impact.
The ideal candidate is a highly proactive, business-minded attorney who enjoys building and evolving governance programs and processes, works well independently and collaboratively, and provides clear, decisive recommendations. The candidate should thrive in a fast-paced, complex environment and collaborate effectively with senior management, IT and cybersecurity teams, business teams, vendors, customers, and outside counsel.
Key Responsibilities
Responsibility #1– 100%
Support Premier’s regulatory compliance with applicable privacy and cybersecurity laws, and related industry frameworks, including proactively monitoring and interpreting developing laws and frameworks.
Provide legal oversight and guidance regarding Premier’s digital compliance risks, including website and application terms & conditions, online tracking technologies, digital accessibility requirements, digital asset disclosures, and employee data access policies.
Support enterprise innovation and growth by incorporating privacy, cybersecurity, and digital compliance-by-design principles from the outset of those initiatives.
Conduct enterprise legal risk reviews across privacy, cybersecurity, and digital matters, including privacy impact assessments, data subject rights requests, supplier privacy reviews, and vendor cybersecurity assessments, and support AI impact assessments involving privacy, cybersecurity, or digital compliance issues.
Contribute to continued modernization and development of Premier’s Digital & Data Legal and Governance organization, digital & data policies and procedures, and overall risk governance framework across privacy, cybersecurity, and digital.
Provide legal counsel for security and privacy incident investigations, mitigations, response, and regulatory reporting, partnering with internal stakeholders and external parties as needed.
Serve the AI & Data Analytics Office and Legal as a primary legal specialist across privacy, cybersecurity, and digital regulatory compliance and risk. Maintain related policies and contract templates, and draft and negotiate specialized or complex contract terms related to those areas.
​Required Qualifications
Work Experience:
Years of Applicable Experience - 7 or more years
Education:
Juris Doctorate  (Required)
Required Certifications/Licensing
Active license in good standing to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, with eligibility to serve as in-house counsel as required.
Preferred Qualifications
Skills:
One or more relevant privacy or AI governance certifications, such as CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT.
Experience operationalizing privacy, AI, and digital risk programs and related processes.
Familiarity with OneTrust, Transcend, or similar privacy or AI governance platforms.
Experience:
At least 5 years of relevant legal experience, preferably 5 to 7 or more years
, advising on privacy, cybersecurity, digital compliance, technology, or related regulatory matters in a law firm, in-house legal department, government agency, or comparable environment.
Substantive knowledge of U.S. privacy and data protection laws
, including HIPAA and HITECH, state comprehensive privacy laws, state consumer health data laws, data breach notification laws, and other requirements governing the collection, use, disclosure, retention, and protection of personal information.
Demonstrated experience interpreting cybersecurity laws, regulations, and recognized cybersecurity frameworks,
including the ability to identify legal, regulatory, and compliance requirements arising under authorities and frameworks such as FISMA, NIST, and PCI DSS and translate those requirements into practical guidance for Cybersecurity, IT, compliance, and business teams.
Hands-on experience conducting or providing legal oversight for privacy and digital risk assessments
, including privacy impact assessments, records of processing activities, data subject request workflows, supplier privacy reviews, vendor cybersecurity assessments, and assessments of new products, technologies, data uses, or business initiatives.
Experience advising on digital compliance matters
, including website and application privacy disclosures, online tracking technologies, cookies and consent requirements, digital terms and conditions, consumer-facing data practices, and accessibility-related legal requirements.
Experience supporting privacy and cybersecurity incident response,
including conducting legal assessments, coordinating investigation and mitigation activities, determining contractual and regulatory notification obligations, preparing, or reviewing notifications, and working with affected business partners, customers, regulators, forensic providers, notification vendors, and outside counsel.
Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating privacy, cybersecurity, and data protection provisions in commercial agreements
, including data processing agreements, business associate agreements, cybersecurity addenda, incident notification provisions, international data transfer terms, and privacy and cybersecurity requirements in customer and supplier contracts.
Experience advising business, product, technology, data, and cybersecurity stakeholders during the design or implementation of new products, services, systems, vendors, and data uses
, with the ability to identify applicable requirements early and recommend practical controls or risk mitigations.
Experience developing, implementing, or materially improving privacy, cybersecurity, or digital governance programs
, including policies, standards, procedures, assessment methodologies, templates, decision records, escalation protocols, training materials, and compliance workflows.
Education:
Juris Doctorate

Be adaptive and change priorities quickly; meet deadlines
Attention to detail
Operate computer programs and software
Ability to communicate effectively with audiences in person and in electronic formats
.
Day-to-day contact with others (co-workers and/or the public)
Making independent decisions
Ability to work in a collaborative business environment in close quarters with peers and varying interruptions

Sedentary work involves remaining stationary most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if movement is required only occasionally, and all other sedentary criteria are met.

rows.title: Senior HR Project Manager
rows.description:
About Carrier
Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit
corporate.carrier.com
or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.
About the Role
We are seeking a proactive, collaborative, and results-oriented
HR Project Manager
to lead critical human resources initiatives that improve how we attract, develop, engage, and retain talent. This role will partner closely with HR leaders, business stakeholders, Centers of Excellence, and cross-functional teams to translate business priorities into well-executed HR programs, scalable processes, and measurable outcomes.
The ideal candidate is a strong project leader and problem solver who can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment, use data to inform decisions, and build alignment across diverse stakeholders. This person will bring a practical understanding of HR programs, change management, process improvement, and employee experience. They will also be strategic and proactive in identifying and prioritizing new projects based on evolving business conditions, organizational needs, and opportunities to improve outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the planning, execution, governance, and evaluation of HR projects and programs aligned to business and talent priorities.
Develop clear project plans, timelines, milestones, communication plans, and success measures to ensure initiatives are delivered on time and with measurable impact.
Partner with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations, HR Technology, Legal, Finance, and business leaders to design and implement solutions.
Support programs related to workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, employee engagement, career development, retention, manager capability, HR process improvement, and organizational change.
Facilitate stakeholder engagement, decision-making, and issue resolution across multiple workstreams and levels of the organization.
Prepare executive-ready updates, dashboards, and presentations that summarize progress, risks, decisions needed, and key metrics.
Use HR data and analytics to identify trends, monitor program effectiveness, and recommend actions to improve outcomes.
Drive change management activities, including stakeholder readiness, communication, training, feedback loops, and adoption tracking.
Identify opportunities to simplify HR processes, improve employee and manager experience, and enable scalable ways of working.
Maintain strong documentation, project governance, and follow-through to ensure accountability and sustainability of HR initiatives.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree.
5+ years of experience in Human Resources, project management, program management, HR operations, or HR transformation
Preferred Qualifications
Post-graduate degree (complete or in-process).
Project management certification or formal training, such as PMP, CAPM, Agile, Scrum, or Lean/Six Sigma.
Experience with Workday or other HRIS platforms, case management tools, reporting dashboards, or HR analytics.
Experience working in a matrixed, global, or multi-site organization.
Demonstrated experience managing complex projects with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and defined deliverables.
Strong understanding of HR processes and programs, such as talent acquisition, onboarding, employee engagement, performance management, talent development, total rewards, HR operations, or HR systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear presentations, status updates, and leadership-ready materials.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with attention to detail and follow-through.
Ability to influence without authority, build trusted relationships, and drive alignment across functions and leadership levels.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and adapting quickly as priorities, timelines, or business needs evolve.
Pay Range
The annual salary for this position is between $117,500.00 - $234,500.00 annually. Factors which may affect pay within this range include, but are not limited to, skills, education, experience, and other unique qualifications of the successful candidate. The pay range will not be below the minimum wage applicable to the jurisdiction in which the applicant is to be employed.
Other Compensation
This position is entitled to short-term cash incentives, subject to plan requirements.
Benefits
Employees are eligible for benefits, including:
Health Care Benefits
: Medical, Dental, Vision; Wellness incentives
Retirement Benefits
Time off and Leave
: Paid vacation days, up to 15 days; paid sick days, up to 5 days; paid personal leave, up to 5 days; paid holidays, up to 13 days; birth and adoption leave; parental leave; family and medical leave; bereavement leave; jury duty leave; military leave; purchased vacation
Disability
: Short-term and long-term disability
Life Insurance and Accidental Death and Dismemberment

rows.description:
About Carrier
Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. ABOUT THIS ROLE
Carrier is seeking a highly skilled Project Manager to oversee our scope of work in data center construction projects. This role is responsible for the startup, commissioning, and field modifications of Carrier air- and water-cooled chillers. The Project Manager will work closely with internal and external teams including engineering, factory operations, field service, commissioning authorities, general contractors, and subcontractors.
The primary job sites are located in the West South-Central region of the United States including Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Louisiana and the surrounding area. Travel from a nearby regional home location is acceptable. Please note that extensive travel for onsite construction project management outside this geography may be required.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Project Execution & Management
Lead startup, commissioning, and field modification processes for Carrier air- and water-cooled chillers in newly constructed data centers.
Develop and manage comprehensive project plans, ensuring schedules and budgets are met.
Track and review key performance indicators (KPIs) to monitor project success.
Conduct progress meetings with stakeholders, addressing design, material delivery, and labor schedules.
Ensure all projects meet or exceed booked profit margin goals.
Work with project coordination to order and track all chiller parts needed for warranty execution.
Stakeholder & Customer Coordination
Collaborate with sales, prime contractors, and end-users to fulfill project scope and deliverables.
Serve as the primary liaison representing Carrier between the customer, commissioning authority, general contractor, and subcontractors, ensuring smooth communication and project progression.
Provide professional, timely resolution for customer concerns, ensuring satisfaction with all aspects of project execution.
Technical Expertise & Compliance
Interpret and apply mechanical, electrical, and architectural drawings to ensure compliance with design specifications.
Ensure adherence to industry codes, standards, and project specifications.
Apply working knowledge of Building Automation System (BAS) integration to ensure proper controls functionality.
Manage the change order process, preventing scope creep and maintaining project integrity.
Financial & Operational Oversight
Accurately forecast monthly revenue by estimating project completion costs.
Manage project documentation, including warranty processing and factory-generated service information in collaboration with our Service Engineering team.
Maintain rigorous job safety standards across all projects.

High school diploma or GED.
5+ years of experience in project management coordinating project schedules, deliverables, and activities involving multiple stakeholders, contractors, vendors, and/or customers; OR  4+ years of experience supporting mechanical, electrical, controls, commissioning, construction, or field service projects.
2+ years reading and interpreting blueprints and technical mechanical systems documents.
Ability and willingness to travel up to 60% of the time within the USA as required by business needs.

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Chemical Engineering; or a Master's degree/MBA.
Data center industry experience with water- or air-cooled chillers.
Commercial HVAC expertise, including centrifugal chillers, Cooling Distribution Unit systems, and airside equipment.

rows.title: Associate Manager, DOT Compliance and Fleet Asset Management
rows.description:
Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.
Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.
Why Campbell’s…
Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s.   Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.
How you will make history here...
The Associate Manager, DOT Compliance and Fleet Asset Management leads DOT compliance, fleet safety administration, regulatory reporting, fuel tax coordination, fleet data accuracy, and operational readiness. The role partners with field teams, internal stakeholders, and external vendors to support safe, compliant, cost-effective, and reliable fleet operations.
What you will do...
•	Lead DOT compliance activities for over-the-road drivers, plant switchers, and sales fleet drivers, including driver qualification files, onboarding and renewal documentation, hours-of-service monitoring, and record retention.
•	Monitor vehicle compliance with federal and state requirements, including registrations, license plates, permits, and renewals.
•	Serve as the primary contact for fleet compliance vendors, reporting, system issues, and required authorizations.
•	Administer drug and alcohol testing requirements, including random testing, new-driver enrollment, completion tracking, and record accuracy.
•	Coordinate driver onboarding and separation activities across fleet compliance systems and maintain required driver, accident, and safety records.
•	Support sales fleet compliance, including driver validation and required documentation.
•	Manage environmental and fleet reporting by collecting, submitting, and reviewing mileage, fuel, vehicle, load, and idle-time information.
•	Coordinate fuel tax reporting and resolve related mileage, fuel, equipment, and data discrepancies within required deadlines.
•	Maintain accurate tractor and trailer records, including vehicle identification, registration, equipment type, location, and asset status.
•	Support fleet technology and equipment by coordinating installation, maintenance, repairs, testing, inventory, troubleshooting, and driver training.
•	Coordinate the purchase, maintenance, and repair of driver safety and material-handling equipment.
•	Partner with the fleet coordinator to review and code fleet-related invoices, validate supporting documentation, and ensure expenses and chargebacks are assigned correctly.
•	Manage underground fuel tank compliance at the Charlotte location, including fuel ordering, inspections, record retention, leak notifications, repairs, and vendor coordination.
•	Lead or support accident investigations, safety documentation, fleet manual updates, compliance reporting, presentations, vendor reviews, and transportation safety initiatives.
Scope of Responsibility
This role helps reduce compliance, safety, operational, and financial risk across private fleet, plant switcher, sales fleet, and site-level fleet operations. The position supports fleet safety standards, regulatory compliance, reporting accuracy, vendor coordination, technology readiness, cost control, and operational continuity. The role works cross-functionally with transportation, sales, field leadership, maintenance, legal, finance, compliance partners, and external vendors.
Who you will work with...
You will work with the transportation/fleet management team and drivers.
It would be great if you have (nice to haves)...
•	Experience in a private fleet, manufacturing, distribution, or multi-site transportation environment preferred.
•	Experience with DOT audits, fleet compliance systems, electronic logging platforms, fuel tax reporting, fleet technology, underground fuel tank compliance, vendor billing, and CDL or private fleet operations preferred.
•      DOT certification
•      Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Transportation, Logistics, Supply Chain, Business Administration, Environmental Health and Safety, or a related field preferred. Equivalent experience and relevant training will be considered.
•	Strong knowledge of federal motor carrier safety regulations, driver qualification requirements, hours-of-service rules, accident recordkeeping, and drug and alcohol testing requirements.
•	Experience with fleet compliance, driver monitoring, fuel reporting, vehicle management, electronic logging, and Microsoft Excel systems.
•	Strong analytical, organizational, documentation, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•	Ability to investigate data discrepancies and resolve compliance issues across multiple systems.
•	Working knowledge of tractors, trailers, onboard technology, fuel systems, and fleet support equipment.
•	Ability to manage recurring regulatory deadlines, maintain accurate records, coordinate with vendors, and make sound decisions that support safety, compliance, cost control, and operational continuity.
•	Knowledge of accounts payable, purchase orders, vendor billing, damage documentation, and cost allocation processes preferred.

The target base salary range for this full-time, salaried position is between
$72,000-$99,000
Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. Total pay may include other forms of compensation. As a Program Manager you will lead the assigned program(s) with an emphasis on New Product Introduction (NPI) for Electro-Mechanical Systems.  As part of NPI structured implementation, you, in conjunction with the Project Engineer, will lead the program through all phases of development of the new product (TIM’s, PDR’s, CDR’s, Qualification, and Transition to Production). You will be the main point of contact for the customer and be directly responsible for Schedule, Cost, and Performance of assigned programs.  You will be required to coordinate with multiple departments and facilities across various geographic locations to assure alignment of customer requirements.

Salary: $130,000 to $150,000
Please note that the salary range information provided is a general guideline only, reflecting a position based in NC. Criteria such as the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience, the scope of the specific position, as well as market and business considerations will be evaluated when extending an offer.

Single point of contact for customer to address all program needs

Coordinate with various departments and/or facilities to implement customer initiatives or prepare for customer reviews
Understand and communicate to all stakeholders the key business contractual items that impact program profitability
Monitor financial health of the program(s) and coordinate action plans with other departments and facilities to execute strategies in support of achieving profitability targets
Development and monitoring of Key Performance Indicators (both external and internal)
Maintain delivery schedules and forecasts for the program(s)
Coordinate and support, as required, proposal efforts, contract negotiations, budget inputs, and management reporting requests
What You Bring
Five (5) to seven (7) years’ experience in aerospace Program Management or Project Engineering.
Five (5) to seven (7) years’ experience leading the development of electro/mechanical systems with an emphasis on circuit design's.
Preference for experience with motorized mechanical actuators and associated electronic controllers for aerospace applications.
Working knowledge of RTCA DO-178 and DO-254 specifications

Makes accurate, timely, and informed decisions

Guides groups or individuals toward common objectives
Demonstrates a sense of urgency about next steps

Forecast needs
Identifies and effectively utilizes appropriate resources

Knowledge of manufacturing mechanical hardware and development of associated electronic controllers
Manages financial data effectively
Travel:
expected up to 20%

Environmental, Social and Governance
Curtiss-Wright Actuation Division designs, manufactures, and supports electro-mechanical actuation products and systems for use in demanding applications in Aerospace, Defense and Industrial Automation markets. Our market leading solutions help improve the reliability, efficiency and performance of our customers' operations and platforms, as well as reducing their environmental impact with energy efficient electro-mechanical designs and technology. For the Aerospace market, we supply actuation systems for flight control, landing gear, utility and other applications on both commercial and military aircraft. In Ground & Naval Defense markets, we support a wide array of applications ranging from door assist, ramp and hatch actuation, weapons handling systems, radar and launch platform actuation, and robotic (AUV/ROV) actuation.

rows.description:

Enjoy a true sense of ownership as you work with a proven industry leader on some of the most exciting and high-profile projects in the nation. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more.
Why Rosendin?
Committed. Innovative. Engaged.
If you're looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding over 100+ years ago, Rosendin has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest

electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We'd love to have you as a shareholder!
Your Next Opportunity:
As our Supplier Quality Program Manager, you will establish and drive a robust program to ensure the quality and reliability of materials and services delivered by Rosendin's supply chain partners. This pivotal role directly impacts our project success, operational efficiency, and reputation for excellence in electrical construction across the nation. You will champion a culture of continuous improvement, fostering strong supplier relationships that uphold our commitment to safety and quality, all while contributing to the shared success of our employee-owned company.
What You'll Do:
Develop, implement, and continuously improve Rosendin's national supplier quality management program, establishing clear standards, processes, and metrics.
Define and communicate supplier quality requirements and performance expectations to internal stakeholders and external supply partners.
Conduct regular supplier audits, assessments, and performance reviews to ensure compliance with Rosendin's specifications, safety standards, and contractual obligations.
Lead root cause analysis and corrective action initiatives with suppliers for non-conforming materials or services, driving timely resolution and preventing recurrence.
Collaborate closely with procurement, project management, engineering, and field operations teams to integrate supplier quality considerations throughout the project lifecycle, from design to installation.
Manage and maintain a centralized database of approved suppliers, including their qualification status, performance records, and audit results.
Develop and deliver training programs for internal teams on supplier quality processes, risk identification, and performance monitoring.
Track, analyze, and report key supplier quality performance indicators (KPIs) to leadership, identifying trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Support the qualification of new suppliers, ensuring their capabilities and quality systems align with Rosendin's requirements.
What You'll Need to Be Successful:
Proven ability to design, implement, and manage comprehensive quality programs within a complex supply chain environment.
Strong understanding of quality management systems (e.g., ISO 9001), methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma), and audit techniques.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with a data-driven approach to continuous improvement.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills to build and maintain effective relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders.
Proficiency in project management principles and tools, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives concurrently.
Knowledge of electrical construction materials, components, and common industry quality standards.
Experience with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems (e.g., Oracle Fusion) and quality management software.
Demonstrated leadership and influencing skills to drive change and achieve program objectives without direct authority over all contributing parties.
What You Bring to Us:
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related technical field.
5-8+ years of progressive experience in supplier quality, procurement, or supply chain management, preferably within the construction, manufacturing, or electrical industry.
Certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) are highly preferred.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing supplier relationships in a program management capacity.
Valid driver's license and an acceptable motor vehicle driving record.
Travel:
Up to 25 - 50% domestic travel to Rosendin offices, job sites, and supplier facilities.
Working Conditions:
Primarily office-based work with occasional visits to job sites and supplier facilities; may involve exposure to varied environmental conditions, including outdoor weather, high noise levels, and construction hazards.
Ability to frequently stand, walk, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, and reach with hands and arms.
Capable of lifting and/or moving up to 25 pounds occasionally and up to 10 pounds frequently.
Use of standard office equipment (computer, phone, copier) and adherence to all Rosendin safety protocols, including wearing appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) when in the field.
