rows.title: Automation & Controls Associate Engineer
rows.description:
The Asahi Kasei Group operates with a commitment of creating for tomorrow.  Our business sectors, Material, Homes, and Health Care, contribute to the development of society by anticipating the changing needs of those around the world. We look for candidates that offer a fresh perspective and a variety of skills to help us achieve our commitment.
We are currently seeking applications to fill the following job opening at Celgard where we develop and manufacture membrane battery separators that are critical components used in lithium-ion batteries for electric drive vehicles (EDVs) and energy storage systems (ESS).
Company:
Celgard, LLC
Job Description:
About the Role
We are seeking an
Automation & Controls Associate Engineer
to be a part of the maintenance team based at Celgard’s Charlotte, NC plant.   This position directly reports to the Plant Maintenance Manager and does not supervise others.  The
Automation & Controls Associate Engineer is responsible for installing, modifying, and servicing process control systems throughout the facility as well as providing electrical engineering support while contributing to electrical designs and drawings. This person will work in a high performance, team-centered work environment to support operations, engineering, and maintenance by driving continuous improvement in the automation and control of the manufacturing. The incumbent will utilize data management skills, PLC (Programmable Logic Control) skills, electrical engineering concepts, and general troubleshooting skills to solve complex manufacturing processes, create enhancements to the process control systems, and provide electrical design solutions.  This position is also responsible for assisting with programming and installation of new equipment during a start-up.
Key Accountabilities
Support equipment installation and modification in coordination with Project and Production Engineering initiatives.
Provide day-to-day support for all software and hardware that comprise the plant control network including PLC’s, drives, switches, PCs, and servers.
Work closely with Manufacturing Technicians, Production Engineers, Project Engineers, and I&E (Instrumentation & Electrical) Technicians to provide advice and support, help diagnose PLC system and process issues, provide electrical design solutions, and lead troubleshooting efforts related to these systems.
Maintain and update SCADA systems, including Inductive Automation Ignition platform, as well as maintain SCADA supervisory systems to analyze process data and create process trend graphs.
Work with vendors of PLC hardware/software & SCADA software to troubleshoot and enhance the performance of equipment.
Work with suppliers of related instruments and electronic equipment related to the PLC equipment. Contact suppliers to clarify performance and application of PLC equipment, instruments, drives, and other equipment that is part of the control systems.
Set up, modify, and analyze alarm and event display and archiving.
Participate in cross-functional continuous improvement teams.
Maintain compliance with all plant safety systems and policies, and applicable laws/regulations.
Utilize lean manufacturing methodologies and problem solving/troubleshooting tools to identify root cause of problem areas in Process Control code, Operator Interface, or hardware and effectively resolve these problems with team member input. Specific troubleshooting and optimization activities will include reducing alarms and unplanned events, minimizing elements in manual, tuning controllers, evaluating the impact of automation systems on plant operability issues, participating in Root Cause Investigations, and utilizing tools such as SPC for optimizing plant Process Control systems.
Qualifications
Required Combination of Education & Experience:
·
Must have the following combination of education and experience:
Bachelor’s degree, preferably in electrical engineering or with technical certification with 1+ years of experience
Associate’s degree, preferably in electrical engineering or with technical certification with 3+ years of experience
High school diploma with technical certification with 5+ years of experience
Required years of experience must include:
Experience with Rockwell (Allen Bradley) PLC programming and software analysis in a manufacturing environment, required
Must possess full-time experience in installing and supporting industrial control systems and control networks including PLC’s, drives, switches, PC diagnostics and repair, and industrial communication protocols
Proficiency with the following control methodologies is required: PID loop configuration and analysis; sequential programming; temperature, pressure, and motor speed control
Proficiency with the following software is required: RS 5000, RS500, and Panel builder
Experience programming and supporting the following platforms is preferred: Mitsubishi PLC’s, Rockwell GuardLogix, Ignition, or demonstrated ability on other high-level scripting language; may also have a combination of Allen Bradley along with these technologies
Must have expertise or demonstrated ability to learn new technology
Other Experience
:
Advanced I&E skills: Capable of using troubleshooting tools and techniques for diagnosing industrial machinery instrumentation, (i.e., Working knowledge of thermocouples, RTDs, pressure and flow transmitters, loops, SCRs and SSRs, encoders, ultrasonic sensors, limit and proximity sensors:  able to troubleshoot wiring from schematics and P&ID able to use multi-meters, amp meters, Fluke calibrator, oscilloscope, pressure calibrator, temperature bath; all strongly preferred
Experience with automated robotic assembly/packing equipment such as FANUC, or experience with other brands, preferred
AutoCAD experience preferred
Ability to read and interpret P&ID drawings, required; ability to edit P&ID drawings preferred
Ability to write technical communications including electrical and control drawings preferred
Ability to perform drive configurations and communication protocols associated with drive systems, as well as troubleshoot drive systems, required
Key Attributes:
Ability to work independently under limited supervision, and provide direction/leadership to others in automation tasks/projects, required
Strengths in organization and motivation, required
Excellent communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills, required
Strong analytical skills to analyze process performance and recommend changes, required
Must be able to recognize inefficiencies in the process
Detail‑oriented execution combined with big‑picture strategic thinking is required
Asahi Kasei and Celgard Values
Sincerity – Being sincere with everyone
Challenge – Bolding taking challenges, continually seeking change
Creativity – Creating new value through unity and synergy
Travel
Must be able and willing to travel up to 5% to the Concord, NC plant to help when needed.
Working Environment
This position is in a manufacturing plant setting that would require working in a production environment around chemicals.  Work will require standing and walking for up to 80% of the time.  Occasionally, this role requires ascending/descending stairs to access work areas or equipment. Lighting and temperature are adequate.  You may be required to
lift up to 30 pounds and/or force necessary to push, pull, or otherwise move objects.
Celgard manufacturing sites are IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 certified.
Perks & Benefits
Comprehensive Healthcare Benefits, effective 1st day of the month
Flexible Spending Account & Health Savings Account
Vacation + 8 Paid Holidays + 24 Hours of Floating Holidays
401K Safe Harbor Contribution + Matching
Paid Parental Leave after a Year of Employment
Employee Assistance Program
Life & Disability Insurances
About Us
For more than 50 years, Celgard has proven itself as a global leader in the development and production of high-performance membrane technology. Celgard specializes in solvent-free, dry-process, microporous membranes used as separators that are a major component of lithium-ion batteries that power a broad range of electric vehicles (EV) and energy storage systems (ESS). Celgard® membrane is also used in specialty applications such as satellites and military installations as well as other barrier-type applications like technical textiles for waterproof and breathable apparel. Headquartered in the United States, we operate manufacturing facilities in the U.S. and China and have sales and technical service staff located strategically throughout North America, Europe, and Asia.
#LI-MN1
As an equal opportunity employer, Asahi Kasei believes a diverse workforce will provide us with the ability to continuously support the changes in the economy, society, and environment.

rows.description:
Field Project Manager - Décor Installation
Bring Brands to Life Across the Nation
At
idX
, we don't just manufacture retail environments, we create immersive brand experiences for some of the world's most recognized retailers. As one of the world's leading retail environment manufacturers and solutions providers, we deliver complex, custom programs that transform customer spaces at scale.
Backed by the strength and stability of
UFP Industries
, idX combines the resources of a global organization with the agility, innovation, and entrepreneurial culture of an industry leader.
We're seeking a hands-on, solutions-driven
Field Project Manager
to lead high-profile décor installation projects across multiple locations nationwide. If you enjoy working in the field, solving problems in real time, collaborating with customers, and seeing projects come to life, this is an opportunity to make a visible impact while building your career with an industry leader.
Travel:
Up to 50% throughout the United States
Why Join idX?
Lead nationally recognized retail and commercial installation programs.
Work directly with major brands and customers.
Enjoy significant autonomy and ownership of your projects.
Partner with engineering, manufacturing, logistics, and project management teams.
Be a key contributor to the successful execution of complex, multi-site installations.
Join a financially strong organization backed by UFP Industries.
Advance your career within a growing national organization.
What You'll Do
As the Field Project Manager, you will serve as the primary on-site representative for idX during décor installations, ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and to the highest quality standards.
Project Leadership & Customer Partnership
Serve as the primary field liaison between customers, store personnel, installation partners, and internal teams.
Represent idX professionally on-site and build strong customer relationships.
Lead installation activities while ensuring alignment with customer expectations and project objectives.
Communicate project progress, field challenges, and solutions to key stakeholders.
Installation Execution & Quality Assurance

Monitor installation quality and ensure all work meets approved specifications and customer expectations.
Conduct site inspections and proactively identify potential risks or challenges.
Oversee project completion and drive the reduction of punch-list items through strong field leadership.
Problem Solving & Continuous Improvement
Troubleshoot installation, engineering, manufacturing, and site-related issues.
Develop practical solutions that keep projects moving forward while minimizing project risk.
Identify root causes of field challenges and coordinate corrective actions with Engineering, Manufacturing, and Project Management teams.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that reduce rework and field-related quality costs.
Contractor & Multi-Site Coordination
Manage and coordinate installation subcontractors across multiple project locations.
Support the qualification and onboarding of new installation partners.
Train installation crews on idX quality standards, processes, and customer expectations.
Monitor subcontractor performance and address installation deficiencies as needed.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Logistics, and Project Management teams.
Participate in prototype reviews and first-article installations as needed.
Identify installation risks early in the project lifecycle to prevent delays and unnecessary costs.
What Makes You Successful
You are a proactive leader who thrives in dynamic environments, communicates effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, and enjoys solving complex challenges in the field.
Education & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Project Management, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
Equivalent combination of field installation, construction, and project management experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

Excellent organizational, communication, customer service, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple projects, and make sound decisions in fast-paced environments.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and Word.
Preferred Qualifications

Background with a retail fixture manufacturer, décor provider, signage company, commercial contractor, or national installation organization.
Knowledge of materials commonly used in décor installations, including wood, metal, acrylic, PVC, glass, graphics, and lighting systems.
Experience coordinating multiple installation crews across geographically dispersed locations.
Familiarity with Microsoft Project and ERP systems.

rows.description:
Agency
Office of the State Controller
Division
Statewide Accounting
Job Classification Title
State Controller Financial Specialist II (NS)
Position Number
60087126
Grade
NC20
About Us
The State Controller serves as an independent resource to protect the financial integrity of the State and to promote accountability in an objective and efficient manner through its accounting, disbursing, payroll, internal controls, data management, eCommerce, and financial reporting systems that serve state agencies, employees, and the public.
The foundational principles of the office are Integrity/Ethics, Objectivity, and Accountability. OSC’s overall goals are to optimize operational execution, manage risk effectively and efficiently, and foster a high-performance culture. OSC will provide excellent customer service while achieving those goals.
Description of Work
NOTE: This job posting will close at 11:59 p.m. the night before the closing date.
Recruitment Range: The Salary Range for NC20 is $70,478-$123,336. Actual salary will be based on selected candidate’s education and experience and available funds for the position.
Please Note: OSC does not use 3rd parties to conduct job interviews.
OSC is interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States.  However, we cannot sponsor visas at this time.
**Successful candidate will be subject to a criminal background check. **
The mission of the Office of the State Controller (OSC) is to protect the financial integrity of the State and promote accountability in an objective and efficient manner.
Description of Work:
OSC is seeking candidates for a State Controller Financial Specialist II position.  This is a full-time position with State Benefits, including health insurance, paid vacation, paid sick time, paid holidays, as well as retirement.  OSC offers 40 hours of continuing professional education (CPE).  Additionally, this position has the capability to be 100% remote.
The position is assigned to the Statewide Accounting Division (SA), Accounting and Financial Reporting Section (AFR) and is a member of the professional team that provides timely, reliable, consistent, and complete financial reports from the North Carolina Financial System (NCFS) for central managers and agency management purposes.  The SA AFR is responsible for the day-to-day accounting policy and procedural control of agencies operating within the NCFS environment.  The section establishes and provides systems control over the NCFS to ensure that all financial transactions are entered, balanced, and reconciled.  The section also researches technical accounting standards and incorporates these standards into financial reporting on the State entity and provides daily, monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting on the financial condition and results of operations of the State entity. The section focuses on State financial reporting and the application of governmental accounting and financial standards, principles, and concepts as set forth by the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB), the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA), the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA), and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).  The AFR section consists of financial specialists who provide accounting policy and procedural support for the agencies operating within the NCFS environment.  The section provides NCFS accounting cycle support, the NCFS chart of accounts, annual generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) conversion to include agency financial statements, Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) funds and notes compilation, development of NCFS statewide accounting system policies and procedures, agency financial systems interface control, NCFS training and implementation support at the agency level, and agency financial systems profile documentation. The Section is also responsible for providing support to the State's agencies and institutions to assure compliance with GAAP and OSC established financial policies and procedures and, to further assure, timely, reliable, consistent, and complete financial information for central managers and agency management purposes.  The section is responsible for producing the State's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) as required by G.S. 143B 426.39 and development of statewide financial policies and procedures that support the financial reporting entity.
Responsibilities:
•	Maintain the North Carolina Financial System (NCFS) for changes to
the State's operating environment.
•	Consult and advise OSC management and agency fiscal staff related
to accounting and reporting issues and solutions.
•	Lead implementation and research activity related to
assigned governmental accounting standards, new legislation, and related
changes to NCFS.
•	Train agency fiscal staff related to accounting and financial reporting
for the State of North Carolina.
•	Develop and document statewide financial reporting policies
and procedures.
•	Review State agency financial reports for compliance with OSC
reporting policies and procedures.
•	Create financial statements and note disclosures included in the
State's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR).
•	Develop and produce interim, annual, and special reports.
Knowledge Skills and Abilities/Management Preferences
Proven, documented skills and ability to apply in-depth knowledge to interpret and implement Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards (GASB); state and federal laws related to financial reporting in the state government environment
Proven, documented ability to apply in-depth knowledge to the development and/or implementation of accounting policy changes
Proven, documented ability to coordinate the development of accounting/financial training and educational opportunities
Proven leadership skills related to working independently on projects within established guidelines and standards
Proven, documented skills in the evaluation of systems of internal control, and the ability to recommend improvements
Minimum Education and Experience
Some state job postings say you can qualify by an “equivalent combination of education and experience.” If that language appears below, then you may qualify through EITHER years of education OR years of directly related experience, OR a combination of both. See the
Education and Experience Equivalency Guide
for details.
NOTE: Transcripts must be uploaded to Workday and attached to your application to receive credit for any training and educational requirements, to qualify for the position.
All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
All work history, training, and education must be listed on the official application, along with attached transcripts, to receive credit.  Applications must be completed in full.  “See Resume” or “See Attached” will not be accepted.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, or a degree in business administration, public administration or a related discipline from an appropriately accredited institution with 18 credit hours of accounting coursework; and three years of accounting experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
EEO Statement
T
he State of North Carolina is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and dedicated to providing employees with a work environment free from all forms of unlawful employment discrimination, harassment, or retaliation. The
state
provides reasonable accommodation to employees and applicants with disabilities; known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions; and for religious beliefs, observances, and practices.

rows.description:

Facility Compliance Consultant I (NS)

60054161
Grade
NC15
About Us
The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is one of the largest, most complex agencies in the state, and has approximately 17,000 employees. It is responsible for ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of all North Carolinians, providing human service needs for special populations including individuals who are deaf, blind, developmentally disabled, and mentally ill, and helping poor North Carolinians achieve economic independence.
Description of Work
The Nursing Home Surveyor (Facility Compliance Consultant I) conducts regulatory inspections of nursing homes to determine compliance with federal and state requirements governing long-term care facilities. This position is responsible for performing routine certification surveys and complaint investigations, evaluating the quality of resident care and facility operations, and documenting findings in accordance with established regulatory standards.
The position prepares survey reports, statements of deficiencies, and complaint investigation findings and provides information regarding compliance requirements to facility staff and administrators.
This home-based position serves Mecklenburg and Cabarrus Counties and requires extensive travel, including occasional overnight travel, weekend work, and evening inspections as necessary to support regulatory activities.
Key Duties Include:
- Conduct routine surveys of nursing homes to evaluate compliance with federal and state regulations governing long-term care facilities.
- Investigate complaints and allegations involving nursing home residents and facility operations to determine compliance with regulatory requirements and identify potential deficiencies.
- Review clinical, administrative, and facility records to assess regulatory compliance, quality of care, and adequacy of services provided to residents.
- Evaluate resident care practices, quality of life measures, facility operations, and service delivery through observation, interviews, and record reviews.
- Document survey and investigation findings and prepare detailed reports in accordance with established regulatory standards and survey protocols.
- Develop statements of deficiencies and complaint investigation findings that accurately identify non-compliance and supporting evidence.
- Communicate survey findings, regulatory requirements, and compliance expectations to facility administrators, management staff, and other stakeholders.
- Maintain accurate and timely documentation of inspections, investigations, findings, and enforcement-related activities using approved reporting systems.
- Participate in required training programs and successfully complete the Federal Surveyor Minimum Qualifications Test (SMQT) following orientation and surveyor training.
- Travel throughout the assigned service area to conduct on-site inspections, including occasional overnight travel, weekend assignments, and evening or night-shift surveys as required.
Knowledge Skills and Abilities/Management Preferences
Salary Grade Range:  $55,221.00-$96,639.00
Recruitment Range:   $55,221.00-$72,100.00
Candidates now meet the minimum qualifications of a position if they meet the minimum education and experience listed on the vacancy announcement.
The Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)/ Management Preferences are not required. Applicants who possess the following skills are preferred:
Proven experience applying a strong clinical nursing background, including assessment, care planning, and delivery of care, to evaluate healthcare services and determine compliance with regulatory standards.
Demonstrated success communicating effectively with healthcare providers, facility staff, residents, families, and other stakeholders regarding clinical, regulatory, and compliance-related matters.
Extensive experience authoring clear, concise, and technically accurate reports, statements of deficiencies, and investigative findings using proper grammar and professional writing standards.
Documented experience analyzing clinical records, resident outcomes, and care practices to identify deficiencies, evaluate quality of care, and support regulatory determinations.
Established expertise interpreting and applying federal and state regulations, policies, and standards while gathering, evaluating, and documenting evidence to support survey, compliance, and enforcement activities.
The Posting Will Close At 11:59 P.M. The Night Before The End Date
This Position Is Funded In Part Through Federal Funds
This Position Is Eligible For A Fully Remote Work Option
This Home-Based Position Serves Mecklenburg And Cabarrus Counties
Physical Requirements:
Ability to sit/stand/walk for prolonged periods
Ability to finger/talk/hear/smell
Ability to lift luggage (20 – 50 pounds)
Close visual acuity.
About the Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR):
The Division of Health Service Regulation oversees medical, mental health and adult care facilities, emergency medical services, and local jails. We check to see that people receiving care in these facilities are safe and receive appropriate care. We make certain that medical buildings are built only when there is a need for them.
About the Nursing Home Licensure and Certification Section:
The Nursing Home Licensure and Certification Section of DHSR regulates nursing homes in North Carolina, including combination homes that have both adult care and nursing home beds. Those receiving Medicare/Medicaid undergo routine federal inspections every nine to fifteen months, conducted by trained healthcare professionals. Surveys review many areas of care and operations, including resident rights, quality of care, staffing, safety, infection control, and emergency preparedness.
The section investigates roughly 3,000 complaints each year, notifying complainants of the findings. When inspectors identify issues, they issue a Statement of Deficiency. The nursing home must submit a correction plan and may face penalties. Inspectors return to ensure all problems are resolved.
Compensation and Benefits:
The State of North Carolina offers excellent comprehensive benefits. Employees can participate in health insurance options, standard and supplemental retirement plans, and the NCFlex program (numerous high-quality, low-cost benefits on a pre-tax basis). Employees also receive paid vacation, sick, and community service leave. In addition, paid parental leave is available to eligible employees.

rows.title: Sr Export Compliance Officer
rows.description:
The Senior Export Compliance Officer is responsible for supporting the execution of global export compliance and sanctions compliance programs by performing first-level trade compliance reviews, sanctions screening activities, and export transaction monitoring. This role serves as a critical interface between business operations, SAP Global Trade Services (SAP GTS), Export Compliance Officers, and Sanctions Compliance teams to ensure transactions are processed in accordance with applicable export control regulations, sanctions requirements, and company policies.
The position plays a key role in reducing compliance risk, maintaining operational continuity, and supporting timely resolution of compliance-related transaction holds and screening alerts.

Sanctioned Party Screening (SPL)
Perform first-level review and disposition of Sanctioned Party List (SPL) screening alerts generated through SAP GTS and related compliance tools.
Conduct due diligence on potential matches by reviewing customer, supplier, consignee, end-user, forwarding agent, and other transaction party information.
Differentiate false positives from potential compliance concerns using established procedures and risk-based assessment criteria.
Escalate confirmed or elevated-risk matches to the Sanctions Compliance Team for secondary review and approval.
Maintain accurate documentation and audit records for all screening activities and determinations.
Monitor screening queues to ensure timely review and resolution of compliance holds.
SAP Global Trade Services (SAP GTS)
Utilize SAP GTS to review and manage SPL, embargo, legal control, and export compliance blocks.
Support investigation and resolution of transaction holds impacting customer orders, deliveries, purchase orders, and shipments.
Coordinate with business stakeholders to gather information required for hold releases and compliance determinations.
Verify data accuracy within GTS and support correction of master data issues impacting compliance screening.
Assist with system testing, process improvements, and user acceptance activities related to GTS enhancements.
Coordination and Stakeholder Support
Serve as a primary point of contact for business users regarding SPL alerts, export holds, and compliance-related inquiries.
Coordinate closely with Export Compliance Officers, Sanctions Compliance teams, Logistics, Customer Service, and Supply Chain organizations.
Facilitate collection of documentation and approvals required to support transaction releases.
Provide guidance and awareness to internal stakeholders on export compliance and sanctions screening requirements.
Support internal and external audit activities through documentation retrieval and compliance evidence preparation.
Compliance Governance & Continuous Improvement
Ensure compliance processes are executed in accordance with corporate policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Monitor trends in screening results and operational metrics to identify improvement opportunities.
Assist in development of training materials, job aids, and process documentation.
Support implementation of process standardization, automation, and efficiency initiatives.

YOU MUST HAVE
Minimum 5+ years of experience in Export Compliance, Trade Compliance, Global Trade Services, Logistics Compliance, or related areas.
Minimum of 1 year of experience working with SAP GTS or similar trade compliance platforms.
Minimum of 1 year of experience performing sanctions screening, restricted party screening, or export transaction reviews.
WE VALUE
Bachelor's degree in International Business, International Trade, Supply Chain, Business Administration, Law, or related field.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Knowledge of U.S. export regulations (EAR, ITAR, OFAC) and international sanctions programs.
Experience supporting global sanctions compliance programs.
Familiarity with denied party screening, embargo reviews, and export licensing concepts.
Experience working in a multinational manufacturing, aerospace, industrial, or technology environment.
Knowledge of SAP ERP integration with SAP GTS.
Experience supporting compliance audits and investigations.

rows.title: Director, Global Risk & Resilience Program Governance
rows.description:
The Global Risk & Resilience Organization establishes and maintains Honeywell's enterprise-wide resilience framework, governance model, policies, standards, and minimum program requirements to ensure the company can effectively prepare for, respond to, recover from, and adapt to operational disruptions.
As the Global Director, Risk & Resilience Program Governance, you will serve as the enterprise leader responsible for the strategy, governance, oversight, and continuous improvement of Honeywell's resilience program, including Business Continuity, Crisis Management, Technology Resilience, and Incident Management Governance. You will define and maintain the enterprise resilience framework, ensuring consistency, accountability, and effective risk management across all Strategic Business Groups (SBGs) and corporate functions and partnering closely with SBG Risk & Resilience leaders who are accountable for implementing and operationalizing the program within their businesses. You will act as a trusted advisor to executive leadership and key stakeholders, ensuring resilience capabilities remain aligned with Honeywell's business objectives, risk profile, and operational priorities.
This role is responsible for establishing minimum program standards, governance requirements, metrics, reporting, training, and maturity expectations for resilience.
Additionally, you will partner closely with Honeywell's Third-Party Cyber Risk and Supplier Resilience leader to ensure suppliers and external partners critical to business continuity are aligned to enterprise resilience requirements and governance expectations, strengthening Honeywell's ability to withstand and recover from third-party disruptions.
You will lead governance of Honeywell’s Global Security policies, standards, and Technical Control Manuals, overseeing their lifecycle to keep requirements current, risk-informed, and aligned with business and regulatory needs. Working with cross-functional stakeholders, you will integrate resilience requirements, monitor compliance and control effectiveness, and drive continuous improvement while enabling the business.

Enterprise Program Leadership
Lead the development, governance, and continuous improvement of Honeywell's enterprise resilience program, including:
Business Continuity
Crisis Management
Technology Resilience
Incident Management Governance
Establish and govern enterprise resilience policies, standards, frameworks, methodologies, and minimum requirements.
Drive the strategic direction, maturity, and continuous improvement of resilience capabilities across the organization.
Ensure resilience programs align with business priorities, regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and emerging risks.
Define and monitor KPIs, KRIs, maturity metrics, and executive reporting to measure resilience performance and risk exposure.
Partner with senior leaders, Enterprise Risk Management, and business stakeholders to strengthen risk management, recovery capabilities, crisis preparedness, and third-party resilience.
Serve as the enterprise resilience governance leader, providing oversight, guidance, tools, best practices, training, and cross-functional collaboration across business units and functions.
Global Security Governance
Own the governance framework supporting Global Security Policies, Standards, and Technical Control Manuals (TCMs), ensuring effective development, review, approval, maintenance, communication, and oversight.
Establish and maintain governance processes that ensure policies, standards, and TCMs remain current, risk-informed, actionable, and aligned with business priorities, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
Lead the enterprise governance lifecycle for Global Security documentation, including periodic reviews, stakeholder engagement, exception management, version control, and executive approvals.
Partner with Security, Cybersecurity, Legal, Compliance, Enterprise Risk Management, Audit, and business stakeholders to ensure governance requirements are consistently understood and implemented.
Define and monitor governance metrics, compliance indicators, and reporting mechanisms that provide visibility into policy adherence, control effectiveness, exception trends, and areas requiring remediation.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives to simplify, strengthen, and mature Honeywell's security governance framework while balancing enterprise requirements with business enablement.
Ensure resilience requirements and governance expectations are effectively integrated into Global Security Policies, Standards, and TCMs where appropriate.

Travel Requirements
Up to 20% domestic and international travel.
YOU MUST HAVE
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering, or mathematics
10+ years of experience leading enterprise resilience, business continuity, crisis management, operational resilience, technology resilience, or risk management programs.
Demonstrated experience designing, governing, and improving enterprise-wide resilience frameworks, policies, standards, and operating models.
Experience working with executive leadership and influencing strategic decisions in large, complex, global organizations.
Professional certification in Business Continuity, Risk Management, Resilience, Crisis Management, (CBCP, MBCI, CBCI, CRMP, DRII).
Proven experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives across multiple business units and regions.
Strong analytical and program management skills, with experience leveraging data and metrics to drive decision-making and program maturity.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills.
Demonstrated experience developing, governing, and managing enterprise policies, standards, control frameworks, and governance processes within a large global organization.
WE VALUE
Deep expertise in Business Continuity, Crisis Management, Technology Resilience, Operational Resilience, and Incident Management.
Experience building and managing enterprise governance programs within a global organization.
Knowledge of third-party risk management, supplier resilience, and critical dependency management.
Strategic mindset with the ability to translate risks into practical, business-focused resilience solutions.
Strong leadership and influencing skills with the ability to drive alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.
Ability to balance enterprise governance responsibilities with practical business needs.
High level of accountability, ownership, and attention to detail.
Passion for organizational preparedness, resilience, and continuous improvement.
Experience leading enterprise governance programs, including policy lifecycle management, standards development, control frameworks, and compliance oversight.

rows.title: Global Risk and Resilience Director, Industrial Automation
rows.description:
The Global Resiliency Organization establishes policies and standards for Resiliency at Industrial Automation (IA) including Business Continuity (BC), Crisis Management (CM), Supplier Resilience (SR) and Technology Resilience (TR).
As the Director of Global Risk and Resiliency, you will play a pivotal role in implementing and optimizing all facets of the Resilience programs, per the Global Resiliency Standards, and augmenting for the IA business. You will report to the
IA Vice President Integrated Supply Chain with a matrix reporting line to the Corporate Governance, Learning, Analytics, Compliance, Risk and Resilience Leader.

Overview of Responsibilities
Implement and continually optimize all aspects of the Resilience programs (BC, CM, SR, TR) globally within IA.
Provide global leadership and guidance for all IA Resiliency matters including the business continuity lifecycle, crisis management, and other resiliency risks.
Review and analyze risk information to identify emerging risks, update risk inventory, and facilitate management’s risk.
Partner with enterprise risk management and senior leadership to develop a comprehensive view of the material business risk including assessment methodology, impacts, mitigation measures and gaps to deliver robust IA enterprise-wide risk management and resilience strategies.
Ensure the effective development of risk assessments, business impact analyses, protection and recovery strategies.
Partner with senior leadership to develop strong working relationships with global IA business and factory leaders, developing a comprehensive view of the business risk/impact, gaps and mitigation.
Accountable for training and exercising the Crisis Management Team, ensuring reporting requirements during any event affecting IA’s global operational capabilities.
Maintain key risk indicators and key performance indications, driving continuous improvement in the business and contributing to the development of the Global Honeywell picture of resilience.
Drive and maintain a governance program aligned with the Honeywell Global Resiliency Policy and Standards that keeps all Honeywell resiliency program components aligned, current, relevant, actionable, auditable, and continually improving.
Develop and maintain a training and awareness program at IA in alignment with the Global Standard and business requirements.
15-30% travel required.

YOU MUST HAVE
8 + years of experience implementing and managing resiliency programs for complex organizations.
Demonstrated leadership experience in the implementation of business continuity, crisis management, supplier resilience and technology resilience in an international manufacturing distribution environment.
Professional certification (DRII, BCI) in business continuity, disaster recovery and/or crisis management.
Demonstrated experience driving complex, cross-functional initiatives at a global level and leading strategic decisions during regional events to assist in crisis response and business recovery efforts.
Demonstrated project management skills, utilizing data to drive decisions and develop maturity in a resiliency program.
Broad understanding of risk-based initiatives and the ability to clearly communicate complex issues and resiliency initiatives.
WE VALUE
Bachelor’s degree in a related field or the equivalent industry experience.
Leadership experience with a high level of accountability and ownership with rigorous attention to detail.

rows.title: Event Operations Manager, Shared Services
rows.description:
The Event Operations Manager will play a critical role in building, operationalizing, and scaling the Event Shared Services organization. This individual will serve as the operational backbone of the events function, driving consistent processes, governance, planning frameworks, tools, reporting, and execution standards across multiple Strategic Business Groups (SBGs).
You will report directly to our Sr. Director of Event Shared Services and work out of our Charlotte, NC global headquarters or our Building Automation headquarters in Atlanta, GA on a hybrid work schedule.
The ideal candidate is a highly organized operations professional with a strong background in event management, program operations, and cross-functional stakeholder engagement. They will partner closely with regional and SBG event leaders, marketing leaders, business group stakeholders, finance, procurement, legal, communications, and external agencies to ensure events are delivered efficiently, consistently, and at scale.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Shared Services Operations & Governance
Design, implement, and continuously improve operational processes that enable a centralized Event Shared Services model.
Establish and maintain event intake, prioritization, resource allocation, and governance frameworks.
Develop standardized operating procedures, templates, playbooks, and workflows that support event execution across all SBGs.
Ensure consistent adoption of event management standards, policies, and best practices.
Drive process optimization initiatives that improve scale, efficiency, and stakeholder satisfaction.
Cross-Functional Partnership
Act as a primary operational liaison between the Event Shared Services team and Strategic Business Groups (SBGs).
Collaborate with marketing, sales, customer success, executive engagement, communications, finance, procurement, and legal teams to support event delivery.
Align stakeholder expectations, timelines, deliverables, and resource requirements across multiple concurrent programs.
Facilitate regular business reviews and planning sessions to assess priorities and operational readiness.
Program & Portfolio Management
Develop and maintain integrated project plans, milestones, dependencies, risk logs, and execution timelines.
Create mechanisms for tracking event demand, capacity planning, and resource utilization.
Monitor event lifecycle performance from intake through post-event reporting.
Systems, Tools & Reporting
Own and optimize event operations tools, platforms, and workflows.
Partner with technology and data teams to improve event management systems and integrations.
Develop dashboards, KPIs, and reporting frameworks to measure event performance, operational efficiency, and business impact.
Produce executive-level reporting and recommendations based on insights and trends.
Budget & Vendor Operations
Support budget planning, forecasting, purchase order tracking, and financial reconciliation processes.
Coordinate vendor onboarding, contract management, and procurement workflows.
Partner with finance and procurement teams to ensure compliance with organizational requirements.
Continuous Improvement
Identify opportunities to streamline operations, reduce manual effort, and improve service delivery.
Lead post-event retrospectives and operational reviews to capture lessons learned and drive improvements.
Champion a culture of operational excellence, accountability, and customer-centric service
In the first 12 months, the Event Operations Manager will be expected to:
Establish scalable operational frameworks supporting all SBG event requests.
Improve planning consistency and stakeholder satisfaction across the event portfolio.
Increase visibility into event demand, resource allocation, and performance metrics.
Reduce operational inefficiencies through standardized processes and automation.
Enable the Event Shared Services organization to operate as a trusted, scalable center of excellence for event delivery across the business.

YOU MUST HAVE
Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Event Management, or related field.
5+ years of experience in event operations, program management, marketing operations, or related disciplines.
Experience supporting enterprise-scale event programs and cross-functional stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated ability to build and implement operational processes and governance models.
Strong project management and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Experience managing multiple complex initiatives simultaneously.
Proficiency with event management, project management, and collaboration tools (e.g., Cvent).
Strong analytical and reporting capabilities.
Travel between 15-25%, depending on event portfolio and business requirements.
WE VALUE
Experience working within a shared services or centralized operations model.
Background supporting executive events, customer engagement programs, or field marketing organizations.
Knowledge of budget management, procurement, and vendor governance processes.

rows.description:

Sr. Construction Manager- Fire Alarm Project Manager
, you will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of multi-year, multisite national programs, managing teams to ensure project schedules, design, execution, testing, closeout, and turnover to service are delivered with consistent quality and speed to satisfy contractual requirements. You will develop mechanisms for monitoring project progress and provide intervention and problem-solving support in partnership with the FAA Sr. Program Manager, project managers, and customers.

Grow the business, manage change, and ensure all contractual obligations are met.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously in a lean administrative environment, demonstrating initiative and accountability. Lead and influence cross-functional teams to ensure contractual deliverables are completed within established timelines.
Coordinate, plan, schedule, and monitor project implementation, including project schedules, budgets, and financial performance.
Manage subcontractor procurement, scheduling, coordination, and performance to ensure project requirements are met.
Apply knowledge of construction dispute resolution processes, contract documents, labor laws, construction contracts, and construction administration to minimize project risk.
Anticipate, identify, evaluate, and negotiate changes to the documented scope of work.
Monitor project progress, identify potential issues, and implement corrective actions to maintain schedules, budgets, and quality standards.
Partner with the FAA Sr. Program Manager, project managers, and customers to resolve project challenges and support successful program execution.
Maintain professional, effective communication with internal stakeholders, customers, subcontractors, and other project partners.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with company policies, reporting requirements, and contractual commitments.
Oversee project testing, closeout, and turnover to service to ensure consistent quality and successful completion.

YOU MUST HAVE
5 or more years of experience in Architecture-Engineering and Design/Build programs.
5 or more years of competitive construction industry experience managing programs or projects exceeding $4 million.
3 or more years of Fire Alarm experience.
Familiarity with NFPA 72, NFPA 101, and fire alarm systems.
Must be a U.S. Person due to contractual and export control requirements.
Ability to complete and pass an FAA background check.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related engineering discipline.
Project Management Institute (PMI) certification.
Certification or experience with XLS140 and XLS3000 Fire Detection, Suppression, and Mass Notification Control Systems.
Xtralis VESDA accreditation.
NICET Level III or higher certification.
Experience managing complex, multisite construction programs and coordinating cross-functional teams.
Strong project planning, scheduling, budgeting, risk management, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication, negotiation, stakeholder management, and subcontractor oversight skills.
Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to changing project requirements, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

rows.description:

Collaborating closely with senior executives and cross-functional teams, you will align IT project strategies with business objectives. With your guidance, we'll navigate the complexities of project management, delivering projects that meet quality, budget, and timeline expectations. If you are a seasoned project management professional with a passion for leading high-performing teams, this role is your gateway to making a significant impact.
You will report directly to our Director of IT Business Partner and you’ll work out of either our Atlanta, GA or Charlotte, NC locations on a Hybrid work schedule.
A highly visible role for an experienced IT professional who excels at partnering with business leaders to drive strategic outcomes. This role is responsible for leading complex IT initiatives, aligning digital IT, ERP and data solutions with business priorities, and ensuring successful delivery of transformation programs that create measurable value across the organization.

o    IT initiatives and transformation initiatives, ensuring alignment with enterprise objectives, timelines, and success measures.

Value Delivery & Outcomes

Stakeholder Engagement & Influence
o    Facilitate decision-making by engaging senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, ensuring clarity, transparency, and alignment.
o    Provide strategic guidance and thought leadership on transformation initiatives, organizational readiness, and process optimization.
•
Organizational Readiness & Adoption
o    Assess business readiness for change and implement targeted strategies to support adoption, focusing on integration into day-to-day operations.
•    Continuous Improvement & Innovation
o    Stay current on emerging technology and industry trends, applying insights to enhance business capabilities and competitive advantage.
o    Drive innovation in delivery approaches, stakeholder engagement, and value measurement.

Project management tools (Jira etc.)
An excellent communicator, facilitator, and presenter, with the ability to engage and influence diverse audiences and stakeholders at all levels.
